lines.text: Μουσάων Ἑλικωνιάδων ἀρχώμεθʼ ἀείδειν,
lines.translit: Mousaōn Helikōniadōn archōmeth' aeidein

lines.translit: orcheuntai kai bōmon eristheneos Kroniōnos

i18n.en: dance, and around the altar of the mighty son of Kronos.

lines.translit: ē Hippou krēnēs ē Olmeiou zatheoio

i18n.en: or in the Horse's Spring, or in holy Olmeios,

lines.translit: akrotatō Helikōni chorous enepoiēsanto

i18n.en: on the highest peak of Helikon they make their dances,

lines.translit: kalous himeroentas eperrōsanto de possin

i18n.en: beautiful, lovely ones, and move nimbly upon their feet.

lines.translit: enthen apornymenai kekalymmenai ēeri pollē

i18n.en: From there they set out, wrapped in thick mist,

lines.text: ἐννύχιαι στεῖχον περικαλλέα ὄσσαν ἱεῖσαι,
lines.translit: ennychiai steichon perikallea ossan hieisai

i18n.en: and walk by night, sending forth their exceedingly lovely voice,

lines.text: ὑμνεῦσαι Δία τʼ αἰγίοχον καὶ πότνιαν Ἥρην
lines.translit: hymneusai Dia t' aigiochon kai potnian Hērēn

i18n.en: singing of Zeus who holds the aegis, and of lady Hera

notes.official: *αἰγίοχος* (aigiochos), Zeus's recurring epithet (also 13, 25, 52), is *aig-* + *-οχος* (< *ἔχω* 'hold, bear'): traditionally 'aegis-holding', the *aigis* being Zeus's storm-shield or goatskin. A minority etymology derives *aig-* not from *αἰγίς* but from the storm-verb *ἀΐσσω* 'to rush, dart' (Chantraine, DELG), without changing the received sense. Evelyn-White's 'who holds the aegis' / 'aegis-holding' is retained, and *aigis* is left untranslated as a fixed cultic object.

lines.text: Ἀργεΐην, χρυσέοισι πεδίλοις ἐμβεβαυῖαν,
lines.translit: Argeiēn chryseoisi pedilois embebauian

i18n.en: of Argos, who walks in golden sandals,

i18n.en: and the daughter of aegis-holding Zeus, bright-eyed Athena,

lines.translit: Phoibon t' Apollōna kai Artemin iocheairan

i18n.en: and Phoibos Apollo, and Artemis who showers arrows,

lines.translit: ēde Poseidaōna geēochon ennosigaion

i18n.en: and Poseidon who holds the earth and shakes it,

lines.translit: kai Themin aidoiēn helikoblepharon t' Aphroditēn

i18n.en: and revered Themis, and quick-glancing Aphrodite,

lines.translit: Hēbēn te chrysostephanon kalēn te Diōnēn

i18n.en: and Hebe of the golden crown, and beautiful Dione,

lines.text: Λητώ τʼ Ἰαπετόν τε ἰδὲ Κρόνον ἀγκυλομήτην
lines.translit: Lētō t' Iapeton te ide Kronon ankylomētēn

i18n.en: and Leto, and Iapetos, and Kronos of the crooked counsel,

notes.official: *ἀγκυλομήτης* (ankylomētēs) of Kronos (also 137, 168) is standardly 'of crooked counsel, wily' — *ἀγκυλο-* 'crooked' + *μῆτις* 'counsel, cunning' (LSJ; West 1966). A folk-association instead links the first element to the *ἅρπη*, the crooked sickle Kronos wields to castrate Ouranos (161–162, 175, 179), giving 'crooked-sickled'; this is a secondary resonance, not the primary sense. Evelyn-White's 'of crooked counsel' is retained; the sickle-pun is noted, not adopted.

lines.text: Ἠῶ τʼ Ἠέλιόν τε μέγαν λαμπράν τε Σελήνην
lines.translit: Ēō t' Ēelion te megan lampran te Selēnēn

i18n.en: and Eos, and great Helios, and bright Selene,

lines.text: Γαῖάν τʼ Ὠκεανόν τε μέγαν καὶ Νύκτα μέλαιναν
lines.translit: Gaian t' Ōkeanon te megan kai Nykta melainan

i18n.en: and Gaia, and great Okeanos, and black Nyx,

notes.official: Name policy for the block: the cosmological theonyms that double as common nouns — Gaia (earth), Ouranos (sky/heaven), Pontos (sea), Nyx (night), and the rest — are transliterated in their Greek forms when personified (Ouranos not Uranus, Kronos not Cronus, Kypros not Cyprus), and glossed as common nouns only where the reference edition does (e.g. 'the earth', 108; 'the wide heaven', 110). Established English collectives are kept (the Muses, the Graces, Desire). See the overlay meta-entry `theogony-name-and-title-conventions`.

lines.text: ἄλλων τʼ ἀθανάτων ἱερὸν γένος αἰὲν ἐόντων.
lines.translit: allōn t' athanatōn hieron genos aien eontōn

i18n.en: and the holy race of the other immortals who are forever.

lines.text: αἵ νύ ποθʼ Ἡσίοδον καλὴν ἐδίδαξαν ἀοιδήν,
lines.translit: hai ny poth' Hēsiodon kalēn edidaxan aoidēn

i18n.en: It was they who once taught Hesiod beautiful song,

lines.text: ἄρνας ποιμαίνονθʼ Ἑλικῶνος ὕπο ζαθέοιο.
lines.translit: arnas poimainonth' Helikōnos hypo zatheoio

i18n.en: as he was shepherding his lambs below holy Helikon.

lines.text: τόνδε δέ με πρώτιστα θεαὶ πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπον,
lines.translit: tonde de me prōtista theai pros mython eeipon

i18n.en: And this word the goddesses spoke to me first of all,

lines.text: Μοῦσαι Ὀλυμπιάδες, κοῦραι Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο·
lines.translit: Mousai Olympiades kourai Dios aigiochoio

i18n.en: the Olympian Muses, daughters of aegis-holding Zeus:

lines.text: ποιμένες ἄγραυλοι, κάκʼ ἐλέγχεα, γαστέρες οἶον,
lines.translit: poimenes agrauloi kak' elenchea gasteres oion

i18n.en: “Shepherds of the field, base things of reproach, mere bellies,

lines.text: ἴδμεν ψεύδεα πολλὰ λέγειν ἐτύμοισιν ὁμοῖα,
lines.translit: idmen pseudea polla legein etymoisin homoia

i18n.en: we know how to speak many false things that resemble genuine ones,

notes.official: Lines 27–28 are the Muses' celebrated self-declaration and a famous crux: *ἴδμεν ψεύδεα πολλὰ λέγειν ἐτύμοισιν ὁμοῖα* / *ἴδμεν δʼ, εὖτʼ ἐθέλωμεν, ἀληθέα γηρύσασθαι* (modelled on *Odyssey* 19.203). Evelyn-White renders both *ἐτύμοισιν* (27) and *ἀληθέα* (28) as 'true things', collapsing a lexical distinction; the translation follows Most (2006 Loeb) in distinguishing *ἔτυμα* 'genuine, real, actual' (27) from *ἀληθέα* 'true, unconcealed' (28) — hence the surface change here, 'like to true things' → 'that resemble genuine ones'. Whether the two words are genuinely opposed or near-synonymous is debated (Puelma 1989; Pucci 1977; Ferrari). The rendering exposes the *ἔτυμα/ἀληθέα* contrast without adopting the stronger claim (that the lines assert the Muses' power to make fiction indistinguishable from truth); that reading — and its bearing on how an inspired tradition may carry truth mixed with plausible falsehood — belongs to the apparatus, not the line.

lines.text: ἴδμεν δʼ, εὖτʼ ἐθέλωμεν, ἀληθέα γηρύσασθαι.
lines.translit: idmen d' eut' ethelōmen alēthea gērysasthai

i18n.en: and we know, when we wish, how to utter what is true.”

notes.official: See on 27. *ἀληθέα γηρύσασθαι* 'to utter what is true': *ἀληθέα* ('un-concealed, true') is rendered 'what is true', kept distinct here from *ἔτυμα* 'genuine' at 27.

i18n.en: So spoke the ready-tongued daughters of great Zeus,

lines.translit: thespin hina kleioimi ta t' essomena pro t' eonta

i18n.en: divine, that I might sing of what will be and what was before,

lines.translit: kai m' ekelonth' hymnein makarōn genos aien eontōn

i18n.en: and they bade me sing of the race of the blessed ones who are forever,

lines.translit: sphas d' autas prōton te kai hystaton aien aeidein

lines.translit: tynē Mousaōn archōmetha tai Dii patri

i18n.en: Come, let us begin from the Muses, who to Zeus the father

lines.translit: hymneusai terpousi megan noon entos Olympou

i18n.en: delight the great mind within Olympos with their singing,

i18n.en: telling of what is, and what will be, and what was before,

i18n.en: in unison of voice; and from them flows the unwearied sound,

lines.translit: deuteron aute Zēna theōn pater' ēde kai andrōn

i18n.en: Second, again, of Zeus, father of gods and of men,

lines.text: ἀρχόμεναί θʼ ὑμνεῦσι καὶ ἐκλήγουσαι ἀοιδῆς,
lines.translit: archomenai th' hymneusi kai eklēgousai aoidēs

i18n.en: they sing both when they begin and when they end their song,

lines.text: ὅσσον φέρτατός ἐστι θεῶν κράτεί τε μέγιστος.
lines.translit: hosson phertatos esti theōn kratei te megistos

i18n.en: how far he is the mightiest of the gods and greatest in power.

notes.official: *φέρτατός … κράτεϊ … μέγιστος*: 'the mightiest … greatest in power.' *φέρτατος* is 'best, foremost, mightiest'; *κράτος* is the poem's key term for sovereign might/dominion — the quality by which Zeus wins and holds rule (73–74), personified as Κράτος 'Might', his enforcer-ally, at 385 (outside this block). Evelyn-White's 'mightiest … greatest in power' is retained; *κράτος* is rendered 'power' and tracked as the Theogony's sovereignty-word.

lines.text: αὖτις δʼ ἀνθρώπων τε γένος κρατερῶν τε Γιγάντων
lines.translit: autis d' anthrōpōn te genos kraterōn te Gigantōn

i18n.en: And again, of the race of men and of the mighty Giants

notes.official: *Γίγαντες* (Gigantes) is rendered 'Giants' with Evelyn-White. The Hesiodic Giants are earth-born (*γηγενεῖς*), sprung with the Erinyes and Meliai from the blood of the castrated Ouranos (185) — a distinct class from the biblical *Nephilim* / *gibbōrîm* of Genesis 6:4 and the Watcher-progeny of 1 Enoch, who are hybrid offspring of divine beings and human women. The Greek word *γίγαντες* is nonetheless the very term the Septuagint uses to render both *Nephilim* and *gibbōrîm* at Genesis 6:4, so it is the shared lexical hinge of the later 'giants' tradition; that translation-history link is comparative apparatus only, not an identity of the two classes. The production glossary's cross-corpus *nephilim-giants* entry is deliberately not extended to the Theogony (see the editor report).

lines.text: ὑμνεῦσαι τέρπουσι Διὸς νόον ἐντὸς Ὀλύμπου
lines.translit: hymneusai terpousi Dios noon entos Olympou

i18n.en: they sing, and delight the mind of Zeus within Olympos,

lines.text: Μοῦσαι Ὀλυμπιάδες, κοῦραι Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο.
lines.translit: Mousai Olympiades kourai Dios aigiochoio

i18n.en: the Olympian Muses, daughters of aegis-holding Zeus.

lines.text: τὰς ἐν Πιερίῃ Κρονίδῃ τέκε πατρὶ μιγεῖσα
lines.translit: tas en Pieriē Kronidē teke patri migeisa

i18n.en: Them in Pieria did Mnemosyne bear, having lain with the father, the son of Kronos,

lines.text: Μνημοσύνη, γουνοῖσιν Ἐλευθῆρος μεδέουσα,
lines.translit: Mnēmosynē gounoisin Eleuthēros medeousa

i18n.en: Mnemosyne, who rules over the hills of Eleuther,

lines.text: λησμοσύνην τε κακῶν ἄμπαυμά τε μερμηράων.
lines.translit: lēsmosynēn te kakōn ampauma te mermēraōn

i18n.en: as a forgetting of evils and a rest from anxious cares.

lines.text: ἐννέα γάρ οἱ νυκτὸς ἐμίσγετο μητίετα Ζεὺς
lines.translit: ennea gar hoi nyktos emisgeto mētieta Zeus

i18n.en: For nine nights wise Zeus lay with her,

lines.text: νόσφιν ἀπʼ ἀθανάτων ἱερὸν λέχος εἰσαναβαίνων·
lines.translit: nosphin ap' athanatōn hieron lechos eisanabainōn

i18n.en: going up into her holy bed apart from the immortals;

lines.text: ἀλλʼ ὅτε δή ῥʼ ἐνιαυτὸς ἔην, περὶ δʼ ἔτραπον ὧραι
lines.translit: all' hote dē rh' eniautos eēn peri d' etrapon hōrai

i18n.en: but when a year had passed, and the seasons had turned round

lines.text: μηνῶν φθινόντων, περὶ δʼ ἤματα πόλλʼ ἐτελέσθη,
lines.translit: mēnōn phthinontōn peri d' ēmata poll' etelesthē

i18n.en: as the months waned, and many days were completed,

lines.text: ἣ δʼ ἔτεκʼ ἐννέα κούρας ὁμόφρονας, ᾗσιν ἀοιδὴ
lines.translit: hē d' etek' ennea kouras homophronas hēsin aoidē

i18n.en: she bore nine daughters, all of one mind, whose hearts are set on song,

lines.text: μέμβλεται ἐν στήθεσσιν, ἀκηδέα θυμὸν ἐχούσαις,
lines.translit: membletai en stēthessin akēdea thymon echousais

i18n.en: and who have a spirit free from care within their breasts,

lines.text: τυτθὸν ἀπʼ ἀκροτάτης κορυφῆς νιφόεντος Ὀλύμπου.
lines.translit: tytthon ap' akrotatēs koryphēs niphoentos Olympou

i18n.en: a little way from the topmost peak of snowy Olympos.

lines.text: ἔνθα σφιν λιπαροί τε χοροὶ καὶ δώματα καλά.
lines.translit: entha sphin liparoi te choroi kai dōmata kala

i18n.en: There are their bright dancing-places and their beautiful halls.

lines.text: πὰρ δʼ αὐτῇς Χάριτές τε καὶ Ἵμερος οἰκίʼ ἔχουσιν
lines.translit: par d' autēs Charites te kai Himeros oiki' echousin

i18n.en: And beside them the Graces and Desire have their homes

lines.text: ἐν θαλίῃς· ἐρατὴν δὲ διὰ στόμα ὄσσαν ἱεῖσαι
lines.translit: en thaliēs eratēn de dia stoma ossan hieisai

i18n.en: in festivity; and sending forth a lovely voice through their mouths

lines.text: μέλπονται πάντων τε νόμους καὶ ἤθεα κεδνὰ
lines.translit: melpontai pantōn te nomous kai ēthea kedna

i18n.en: they sing, and celebrate the ordinances of all and the goodly ways

lines.text: ἀθανάτων κλείουσιν, ἐπήρατον ὄσσαν ἱεῖσαι.
lines.translit: athanatōn kleiousin epēraton ossan hieisai

i18n.en: of the immortals, sending forth their lovely voice.

lines.text: αἳ τότʼ ἴσαν πρὸς Ὄλυμπον ἀγαλλόμεναι ὀπὶ καλῇ,
lines.translit: hai tot' isan pros Olympon agallomenai opi kalē

i18n.en: They then went to Olympos, glorying in their beautiful voice,

lines.text: ἀμβροσίῃ μολπῇ· περὶ δʼ ἴαχε γαῖα μέλαινα
lines.translit: ambrosiē molpē peri d' iache gaia melaina

i18n.en: with immortal song; and the black earth rang around them

lines.text: ὑμνεύσαις, ἐρατὸς δὲ ποδῶν ὕπο δοῦπος ὀρώρει
lines.translit: hymneusais eratos de podōn hypo doupos orōrei

i18n.en: as they sang, and a lovely sound rose up beneath their feet

lines.text: νισσομένων πατέρʼ εἰς ὅν· ὃ δʼ οὐρανῷ ἐμβασιλεύει,
lines.translit: nissomenōn pater' eis hon ho d' ouranō embasileuei

i18n.en: as they went to their father; and he reigns in heaven,

lines.text: αὐτὸς ἔχων βροντὴν ἠδʼ αἰθαλόεντα κεραυνόν,
lines.translit: autos echōn brontēn ēd' aithaloenta keraunon

i18n.en: himself holding the thunder and the blazing thunderbolt,

lines.text: κάρτει νικήσας πατέρα Κρόνον· εὖ δὲ ἕκαστα
lines.translit: kartei nikēsas patera Kronon eu de hekasta

i18n.en: having conquered by might his father Kronos; and well

lines.text: ἀθανάτοις διέταξεν ὁμῶς καὶ ἐπέφραδε τιμάς.
lines.translit: athanatois dietaxen homōs kai epephrade timas

i18n.en: he ordered all things among the immortals alike and appointed their honors.

lines.text: ταῦτʼ ἄρα Μοῦσαι ἄειδον, Ὀλύμπια δώματʼ ἔχουσαι,
lines.translit: taut' ara Mousai aeidon Olympia dōmat' echousai

i18n.en: These things, then, the Muses sang, who have their homes on Olympos,

lines.text: ἐννέα θυγατέρες μεγάλου Διὸς ἐκγεγαυῖαι,
lines.translit: ennea thygateres megalou Dios ekgegauiai

i18n.en: the nine daughters born of great Zeus,

lines.text: Κλειώ τʼ Εὐτέρπη τε Θάλειά τε Μελπομένη τε
lines.translit: Kleiō t' Euterpē te Thaleia te Melpomenē te

i18n.en: Kleio, and Euterpe, and Thaleia, and Melpomene,

lines.text: Τερψιχόρη τʼ Ἐρατώ τε Πολύμνιά τʼ Οὐρανίη τε
lines.translit: Terpsichorē t' Eratō te Polymnia t' Ouraniē te

i18n.en: and Terpsichore, and Erato, and Polymnia, and Ourania,

lines.text: Καλλιόπη θʼ· ἣ δὲ προφερεστάτη ἐστὶν ἁπασέων.
lines.translit: Kalliopē th' hē de propherestatē estin hapaseōn

i18n.en: and Kalliope, who is the foremost of them all.

lines.text: ἣ γὰρ καὶ βασιλεῦσιν ἅμʼ αἰδοίοισιν ὀπηδεῖ.
lines.translit: hē gar kai basileusin ham' aidoioisin opēdei

i18n.en: For she attends upon revered kings as well.

lines.text: ὅν τινα τιμήσωσι Διὸς κοῦραι μεγάλοιο
lines.translit: hon tina timēsōsi Dios kourai megaloio

i18n.en: Whomever the daughters of great Zeus honor,

lines.text: γεινόμενόν τε ἴδωσι διοτρεφέων βασιλήων,
lines.translit: geinomenon te idōsi diotrepheōn basilēōn

i18n.en: and behold at his birth, of the kings nurtured by Zeus,

lines.text: τῷ μὲν ἐπὶ γλώσσῃ γλυκερὴν χείουσιν ἐέρσην,
lines.translit: tō men epi glōssē glykerēn cheiousin eersēn

i18n.en: on his tongue they pour sweet dew,

lines.text: τοῦ δʼ ἔπεʼ ἐκ στόματος ῥεῖ μείλιχα· οἱ δέ τε λαοὶ
lines.translit: tou d' epe' ek stomatos rhei meilicha hoi de te laoi

i18n.en: and from his mouth flow gentle words; and the people,

lines.text: πάντες ἐς αὐτὸν ὁρῶσι διακρίνοντα θέμιστας
lines.translit: pantes es auton horōsi diakrinonta themistas

i18n.en: all of them, look to him as he decides disputes

lines.text: ἰθείῃσι δίκῃσιν· ὃ δʼ ἀσφαλέως ἀγορεύων
lines.translit: itheiēsi dikēsin ho d' asphaleōs agoreuōn

i18n.en: with straight judgments; and he, speaking without stumbling,

lines.text: αἶψά κε καὶ μέγα νεῖκος ἐπισταμένως κατέπαυσεν·
lines.translit: aipsa ke kai mega neikos epistamenōs katepausen

i18n.en: quickly and skillfully makes an end even of a great quarrel.

lines.text: τοὔνεκα γὰρ βασιλῆες ἐχέφρονες, οὕνεκα λαοῖς
lines.translit: touneka gar basilēes echephrones houneka laois

i18n.en: For this is why kings are prudent: because, when the people

lines.text: βλαπτομένοις ἀγορῆφι μετάτροπα ἔργα τελεῦσι
lines.translit: blaptomenois agorēphi metatropa erga teleusi

i18n.en: are being wronged in the assembly, they bring the deeds to a turnabout

lines.text: ῥηιδίως, μαλακοῖσι παραιφάμενοι ἐπέεσσιν.
lines.translit: rhēidiōs malakoisi paraiphamenoi epeessin

i18n.en: with ease, winning them over with gentle words.

lines.text: ἐρχόμενον δʼ ἀνʼ ἀγῶνα θεὸν ὣς ἱλάσκονται
lines.translit: erchomenon d' an' agōna theon hōs hilaskontai

i18n.en: And as he comes through the gathering, they seek his favor like a god

lines.text: αἰδοῖ μειλιχίῃ, μετὰ δὲ πρέπει ἀγρομένοισιν·
lines.translit: aidoi meilichiē meta de prepei agromenoisin

i18n.en: with gentle reverence, and he stands out among the assembled.

lines.text: τοίη Μουσάων ἱερὴ δόσις ἀνθρώποισιν.
lines.translit: toiē Mousaōn hierē dosis anthrōpoisin

i18n.en: Such is the holy gift of the Muses to men.

lines.text: ἐκ γάρ τοι Μουσέων καὶ ἑκηβόλου Ἀπόλλωνος
lines.translit: ek gar toi Mouseōn kai hekēbolou Apollōnos

i18n.en: For it is from the Muses and far-shooting Apollo

lines.text: ἄνδρες ἀοιδοὶ ἔασιν ἐπὶ χθόνα καὶ κιθαρισταί,
lines.translit: andres aoidoi easin epi chthona kai kitharistai

i18n.en: that there are singers and harpers upon the earth,

lines.text: ἐκ δὲ Διὸς βασιλῆες· ὃ δʼ ὄλβιος, ὅν τινα Μοῦσαι
lines.translit: ek de Dios basilēes ho d' olbios hon tina Mousai

i18n.en: but from Zeus come kings; and happy is he whom the Muses

lines.text: φίλωνται· γλυκερή οἱ ἀπὸ στόματος ῥέει αὐδή.
lines.translit: philōntai glykerē hoi apo stomatos rheei audē

i18n.en: love; sweet flows the voice from his mouth.

lines.text: εἰ γάρ τις καὶ πένθος ἔχων νεοκηδέι θυμῷ
lines.translit: ei gar tis kai penthos echōn neokēdei thymō

i18n.en: For even if someone with grief in his newly-troubled heart

lines.text: ἄζηται κραδίην ἀκαχήμενος, αὐτὰρ ἀοιδὸς
lines.translit: azētai kradiēn akachēmenos autar aoidos

i18n.en: pines away, sorrowing in his heart, yet when a singer,

lines.text: Μουσάων θεράπων κλέεα προτέρων ἀνθρώπων
lines.translit: Mousaōn therapōn kleea proterōn anthrōpōn

i18n.en: the servant of the Muses, sings the glorious deeds of the men of old

lines.text: ὑμνήσῃ μάκαράς τε θεούς, οἳ Ὄλυμπον ἔχουσιν,
lines.translit: hymnēsē makaras te theous hoi Olympon echousin

i18n.en: and the blessed gods who hold Olympos,

lines.text: αἶψʼ ὅ γε δυσφροσυνέων ἐπιλήθεται οὐδέ τι κηδέων
lines.translit: aips' ho ge dysphrosyneōn epilēthetai oude ti kēdeōn

i18n.en: at once he forgets his heaviness and remembers his cares

lines.text: μέμνηται· ταχέως δὲ παρέτραπε δῶρα θεάων.
lines.translit: memnētai tacheōs de paretrape dōra theaōn

i18n.en: no more; quickly the gifts of the goddesses turn him from them.

lines.text: χαίρετε, τέκνα Διός, δότε δʼ ἱμερόεσσαν ἀοιδήν.
lines.translit: chairete tekna Dios dote d' himeroessan aoidēn

i18n.en: Hail, children of Zeus! and grant me lovely song.

lines.text: κλείετε δʼ ἀθανάτων ἱερὸν γένος αἰὲν ἐόντων,
lines.translit: kleiete d' athanatōn hieron genos aien eontōn

i18n.en: Celebrate the holy race of the immortals who are forever,

lines.text: οἳ Γῆς τʼ ἐξεγένοντο καὶ Οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος,
lines.translit: hoi Gēs t' exegenonto kai Ouranou asteroentos

i18n.en: who were born of Gaia and starry Ouranos,

notes.official: In the proem's second invocation 'Gaia and starry Ouranos' names the divine parental pair by anticipation (cf. 45); the personification proper begins at 126–127. The Greek genitive here is *Γῆς* (Gē), normalized throughout to the standard transliteration Gaia. See on 110.

lines.text: Νυκτός τε δνοφερῆς, οὕς θʼ ἁλμυρὸς ἔτρεφε Πόντος.
lines.translit: Nyktos te dnopherēs hous th' halmyros etrephe Pontos

i18n.en: and of dark Nyx, and those whom the salt Pontos nourished.

lines.text: εἴπατε δʼ, ὡς τὰ πρῶτα θεοὶ καὶ γαῖα γένοντο
lines.translit: eipate d' hōs ta prōta theoi kai gaia genonto

i18n.en: Tell how, at the first, the gods and the earth came to be,

notes.official: *γαῖα* here (*ὡς τὰ πρῶτα θεοὶ καὶ γαῖα γένοντο*, 'how the gods and the earth came to be') stands in a physical catalogue — gods, earth, rivers, sea, stars, heaven (108–110) — and is rendered as the common noun 'the earth' with Evelyn-White, not the goddess Gaia. The register is genuinely ambiguous, since the same *γαῖα* is personified and born as a deity nine lines later (117); the catalogue-context favours the physical sense here. Cf. the clearly common-noun *γαῖα μέλαινα* 'black earth' at 69.

lines.text: καὶ ποταμοὶ καὶ πόντος ἀπείριτος, οἴδματι θυίων,
lines.translit: kai potamoi kai pontos apeiritos oidmati thyiōn

i18n.en: and the rivers, and the boundless sea raging with its swell,

lines.text: ἄστρα τε λαμπετόωντα καὶ οὐρανὸς εὐρὺς ὕπερθεν
lines.translit: astra te lampetoōnta kai ouranos eurys hyperthen

i18n.en: and the shining stars, and the wide heaven above,

notes.official: *οὐρανὸς εὐρὺς ὕπερθεν* 'the wide heaven above' (like 'reigns in heaven', 71) is the common noun 'sky/heaven', as in Evelyn-White. The word becomes the personified god Ouranos only at 126–127, where Gaia bears him 'equal to herself … that he might cover her all about'; from 133 he acts as her consort. In the proem (45, 106) 'Gaia and Ouranos' already names the divine parental pair by anticipation. The personification onset is thus fixed at 126–127, and 71/110 remain physical.

lines.text: οἵ τʼ ἐκ τῶν ἐγένοντο θεοί, δωτῆρες ἐάων
lines.translit: hoi t' ek tōn egenonto theoi dōtēres eaōn

i18n.en: and the gods who were born from them, givers of good things;

notes.official: Line 111 is bracketed (athetized) in the Perseus/Evelyn-White edition: it repeats line 46 verbatim (*οἵ τʼ ἐκ τῶν ἐγένοντο θεοί, δωτῆρες ἐάων*) and is widely judged an interpolation carried over from the earlier passage (West 1966). Per project convention the transmitted line is retained and translated; the athetesis is recorded in the apparatus rather than the surface.

lines.text: ὥς τʼ ἄφενος δάσσαντο καὶ ὡς τιμὰς διέλοντο
lines.translit: hōs t' aphenos dassanto kai hōs timas dielonto

i18n.en: and how they divided their wealth and apportioned their honors,

lines.text: ἠδὲ καὶ ὡς τὰ πρῶτα πολύπτυχον ἔσχον Ὄλυμπον.
lines.translit: ēde kai hōs ta prōta polyptychon eschon Olympon

i18n.en: and also how, at the first, they took possession of many-folded Olympos.

lines.text: ταῦτά μοι ἔσπετε Μοῦσαι, Ὀλύμπια δώματʼ ἔχουσαι
lines.translit: tauta moi espete Mousai Olympia dōmat' echousai

i18n.en: These things tell me, Muses who have your homes on Olympos,

lines.text: ἐξ ἀρχῆς, καὶ εἴπαθʼ, ὅ τι πρῶτον γένετʼ αὐτῶν.
lines.translit: ex archēs kai eipath' ho ti prōton genet' autōn

i18n.en: from the beginning, and tell which of them came to be first.

lines.text: ἦ τοι μὲν πρώτιστα Χάος γένετʼ, αὐτὰρ ἔπειτα
lines.translit: ē toi men prōtista Chaos genet' autar epeita

i18n.en: Truly, first of all Chaos came to be, but next

notes.official: *Χάος* (Chaos) is kept transliterated, its sense fixed by etymology, not by the later popular meaning. From the root *χα-* (*χαίνω/χάσκω* 'to gape, yawn'), Hesiod's Chaos is the primordial 'gap, chasm, yawning void' that comes to be first (West 1966; Kirk–Raven–Schofield 1983) — a spatial opening, emphatically not the post-classical 'disordered confused mass' of Ovid's *Metamorphoses*. Note too that Chaos *γένετο* 'came to be' spontaneously: Hesiod's cosmogony opens with no creator and no act of creation, a structural contrast with creator-cosmogonies that is left to the comparative apparatus.

lines.text: Γαῖʼ εὐρύστερνος, πάντων ἕδος ἀσφαλὲς αἰεὶ
lines.translit: Gai' eurysternos pantōn hedos asphales aiei

i18n.en: wide-bosomed Gaia, the ever-sure seat of all

lines.text: ἀθανάτων, οἳ ἔχουσι κάρη νιφόεντος Ὀλύμπου,
lines.translit: athanatōn hoi echousi karē niphoentos Olympou

i18n.en: the immortals who hold the peak of snowy Olympos,

notes.official: Line 118 is bracketed in the Perseus/Evelyn-White edition and suspected by editors as an interpolated expansion of the 'seat of the immortals' formula (cf. 128). It is retained and translated per project convention, the athetesis noted here.

lines.text: Τάρταρά τʼ ἠερόεντα μυχῷ χθονὸς εὐρυοδείης,
lines.translit: Tartara t' ēeroenta mychō chthonos euryodeiēs

i18n.en: and misty Tartaros in the recess of the wide-wayed earth,

lines.text: ἠδʼ Ἔρος, ὃς κάλλιστος ἐν ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσι,
lines.translit: ēd' Eros hos kallistos en athanatoisi theoisi

i18n.en: and Eros, who is fairest among the immortal gods,

notes.official: *Ἔρος* (Eros) at 120 is one of the first entities to come to be — after Chaos, Gaia, and Tartaros, and before any sexual genealogy — and is kept transliterated with Evelyn-White rather than translated 'Love' or 'Desire'. Here Eros is a primordial cosmogonic principle, the power of attraction and generation that will drive the pairings of the following theogony (West 1966; Kirk–Raven–Schofield 1983), the *λυσιμελής* 'limb-loosener' that 'overpowers the mind' of gods and men (121–122). He is to be distinguished from the later Eros who attends the new-born Aphrodite (201) and, in post-Hesiodic tradition, becomes her son. Rendering him as an abstract 'force' would over-determine; the cosmogonic role is marked here, not imported into the line.

lines.text: λυσιμελής, πάντων δὲ θεῶν πάντων τʼ ἀνθρώπων
lines.translit: lysimelēs pantōn de theōn pantōn t' anthrōpōn

i18n.en: the limb-loosener, who of all gods and all men

lines.text: δάμναται ἐν στήθεσσι νόον καὶ ἐπίφρονα βουλήν.
lines.translit: damnatai en stēthessi noon kai epiphrona boulēn

i18n.en: overpowers the mind and prudent counsel in their breasts.

lines.text: ἐκ Χάεος δʼ Ἔρεβός τε μέλαινά τε Νὺξ ἐγένοντο·
lines.translit: ek Chaeos d' Erebos te melaina te Nyx egenonto

i18n.en: From Chaos came Erebos and black Nyx;

notes.official: *ἐκ Χάεος* 'from Chaos': the primordial gap now generates Erebos and black Nyx. See on 116 for the 'gap/chasm/void' sense of *Χάος*.

lines.text: Νυκτὸς δʼ αὖτʼ Αἰθήρ τε καὶ Ἡμέρη ἐξεγένοντο,
lines.translit: Nyktos d' aut' Aithēr te kai Hēmerē exegenonto

i18n.en: and from Nyx, in turn, came Aither and Hemera,

lines.text: οὓς τέκε κυσαμένη Ἐρέβει φιλότητι μιγεῖσα.
lines.translit: hous teke kysamenē Erebei philotēti migeisa

i18n.en: whom she conceived and bore, having lain in love with Erebos.

lines.text: Γαῖα δέ τοι πρῶτον μὲν ἐγείνατο ἶσον ἑαυτῇ
lines.translit: Gaia de toi prōton men egeinato ison heautē

i18n.en: And Gaia first of all bore, equal to herself,

lines.text: Οὐρανὸν ἀστερόενθʼ, ἵνα μιν περὶ πάντα καλύπτοι,
lines.translit: Ouranon asteroenth' hina min peri panta kalyptoi

i18n.en: starry Ouranos, that he might cover her all about,

notes.official: Here Ouranos first becomes a personified deity: Gaia bears him 'equal to herself … that he might cover her all about' (126–128). This fixes the onset of personification; before this (71, 110) *οὐρανός* is the physical sky. See on 110.

lines.text: ὄφρʼ εἴη μακάρεσσι θεοῖς ἕδος ἀσφαλὲς αἰεί.
lines.translit: ophr' eiē makaressi theois hedos asphales aiei

i18n.en: so that he might be an ever-sure seat for the blessed gods.

lines.text: γείνατο δʼ Οὔρεα μακρά, θεῶν χαρίεντας ἐναύλους,
lines.translit: geinato d' Ourea makra theōn charientas enaulous

i18n.en: And she bore the long Mountains, graceful haunts of the goddesses,

lines.text: Νυμφέων, αἳ ναίουσιν ἀνʼ οὔρεα βησσήεντα.
lines.translit: Nympheōn hai naiousin an' ourea bēssēenta

i18n.en: the Nymphs who dwell among the wooded mountains.

lines.text: ἣ δὲ καὶ ἀτρύγετον πέλαγος τέκεν, οἴδματι θυῖον,
lines.translit: hē de kai atrygeton pelagos teken oidmati thyion

i18n.en: And she also bore the barren sea, raging with its swell,

lines.text: Πόντον, ἄτερ φιλότητος ἐφιμέρου· αὐτὰρ ἔπειτα
lines.translit: Ponton ater philotētos ephimerou autar epeita

i18n.en: Pontos, without sweet love; but afterward,

lines.text: Οὐρανῷ εὐνηθεῖσα τέκʼ Ὠκεανὸν βαθυδίνην,
lines.translit: Ouranō eunētheisa tek' Ōkeanon bathydinēn

i18n.en: having lain with Ouranos, she bore deep-eddying Okeanos,

lines.text: Κοῖόν τε Κρῖόν θʼ Ὑπερίονά τʼ Ἰαπετόν τε
lines.translit: Koion te Krion th' Hyperiona t' Iapeton te

i18n.en: and Koios, and Krios, and Hyperion, and Iapetos,

lines.text: Θείαν τε Ῥείαν τε Θέμιν τε Μνημοσύνην τε
lines.translit: Theian te Rheian te Themin te Mnēmosynēn te

i18n.en: and Theia, and Rhea, and Themis, and Mnemosyne,

lines.text: Φοίβην τε χρυσοστέφανον Τηθύν τʼ ἐρατεινήν.
lines.translit: Phoibēn te chrysostephanon Tēthyn t' erateinēn

i18n.en: and Phoibe of the golden crown, and lovely Tethys.

lines.text: τοὺς δὲ μέθʼ ὁπλότατος γένετο Κρόνος ἀγκυλομήτης,
lines.translit: tous de meth' hoplotatos geneto Kronos ankylomētēs

i18n.en: And after them was born Kronos, youngest, of the crooked counsel,

lines.text: δεινότατος παίδων· θαλερὸν δʼ ἤχθηρε τοκῆα.
lines.translit: deinotatos paidōn thaleron d' ēchthēre tokēa

i18n.en: the most terrible of her children; and he hated his vigorous father.

lines.text: γείνατο δʼ αὖ Κύκλωπας ὑπέρβιον ἦτορ ἔχοντας,
lines.translit: geinato d' au Kyklōpas hyperbion ētor echontas

i18n.en: And again she bore the Kyklopes, who have overweening hearts,

lines.text: Βρόντην τε Στερόπην τε καὶ Ἄργην ὀβριμόθυμον,
lines.translit: Brontēn te Steropēn te kai Argēn obrimothymon

i18n.en: Brontes, and Steropes, and stubborn-hearted Arges,

lines.text: οἳ Ζηνὶ βροντήν τε δόσαν τεῦξάν τε κεραυνόν.
lines.translit: hoi Zēni brontēn te dosan teuxan te keraunon

i18n.en: who gave thunder to Zeus and fashioned the thunderbolt.

lines.text: οἳ δή τοι τὰ μὲν ἄλλα θεοῖς ἐναλίγκιοι ἦσαν,
lines.translit: hoi dē toi ta men alla theois enalinkioi ēsan

i18n.en: In all else they were like the gods,

lines.text: μοῦνος δʼ ὀφθαλμὸς μέσσῳ ἐνέκειτο μετώπῳ.
lines.translit: mounos d' ophthalmos messō enekeito metōpō

i18n.en: but a single eye lay in the middle of their foreheads.

lines.text: Κύκλωπες δʼ ὄνομʼ ἦσαν ἐπώνυμον, οὕνεκʼ ἄρα σφέων
lines.translit: Kyklōpes d' onom' ēsan epōnymon hounek' ara spheōn

i18n.en: Kyklopes was their name, given for this reason: because

lines.text: κυκλοτερὴς ὀφθαλμὸς ἕεις ἐνέκειτο μετώπῳ·
lines.translit: kykloterēs ophthalmos heeis enekeito metōpō

i18n.en: a single circular eye lay in their foreheads;

lines.text: ἰσχὺς δʼ ἠδὲ βίη καὶ μηχαναὶ ἦσαν ἐπʼ ἔργοις.
lines.translit: ischys d' ēde biē kai mēchanai ēsan ep' ergois

i18n.en: and strength and force and craft were in their works.

lines.text: ἄλλοι δʼ αὖ Γαίης τε καὶ Οὐρανοῦ ἐξεγένοντο
lines.translit: alloi d' au Gaiēs te kai Ouranou exegenonto

i18n.en: And again, three other sons were born of Gaia and Ouranos,

lines.text: τρεῖς παῖδες μεγάλοι τε καὶ ὄβριμοι, οὐκ ὀνομαστοί,
lines.translit: treis paides megaloi te kai obrimoi ouk onomastoi

i18n.en: great and mighty, not to be named,

lines.text: Κόττος τε Βριάρεώς τε Γύης θʼ, ὑπερήφανα τέκνα.
lines.translit: Kottos te Briareōs te Gyēs th' hyperēphana tekna

i18n.en: Kottos, and Briareos, and Gyes, arrogant children.

lines.text: τῶν ἑκατὸν μὲν χεῖρες ἀπʼ ὤμων ἀίσσοντο,
lines.translit: tōn hekaton men cheires ap' ōmōn aissonto

i18n.en: From their shoulders sprang a hundred arms,

lines.text: ἄπλαστοι, κεφαλαὶ δὲ ἑκάστῳ πεντήκοντα
lines.translit: aplastoi kephalai de hekastō pentēkonta

i18n.en: not to be approached, and to each fifty heads

lines.text: ἐξ ὤμων ἐπέφυκον ἐπὶ στιβαροῖσι μέλεσσιν·
lines.translit: ex ōmōn epephykon epi stibaroisi melessin

i18n.en: grew from their shoulders upon their sturdy limbs;

lines.text: ἰσχὺς δʼ ἄπλητος κρατερὴ μεγάλῳ ἐπὶ εἴδει.
lines.translit: ischys d' aplētos kraterē megalō epi eidei

i18n.en: and irresistible strength was mighty upon their huge form.

lines.text: ὅσσοι γὰρ Γαίης τε καὶ Οὐρανοῦ ἐξεγένοντο,
lines.translit: hossoi gar Gaiēs te kai Ouranou exegenonto

i18n.en: For all those who were born of Gaia and Ouranos,

lines.text: δεινότατοι παίδων, σφετέρῳ δʼ ἤχθοντο τοκῆι
lines.translit: deinotatoi paidōn spheterō d' ēchthonto tokēi

i18n.en: the most terrible of children, were hated by their own father

lines.text: ἐξ ἀρχῆς· καὶ τῶν μὲν ὅπως τις πρῶτα γένοιτο,
lines.translit: ex archēs kai tōn men hopōs tis prōta genoito

i18n.en: from the beginning; and as soon as each of them was born,

lines.text: πάντας ἀποκρύπτασκε, καὶ ἐς φάος οὐκ ἀνίεσκε,
lines.translit: pantas apokryptaske kai es phaos ouk anieske

i18n.en: he would hide them all away and not let them into the light,

lines.text: Γαίης ἐν κευθμῶνι, κακῷ δʼ ἐπετέρπετο ἔργῳ
lines.translit: Gaiēs en keuthmōni kakō d' epeterpeto ergō

i18n.en: in a hollow of Gaia; and in his evil deed he took delight,

lines.text: Οὐρανός. ἣ δʼ ἐντὸς στοναχίζετο Γαῖα πελώρη
lines.translit: Ouranos hē d' entos stonachizeto Gaia pelōrē

i18n.en: Ouranos did. But huge Gaia groaned within,

lines.text: στεινομένη· δολίην δὲ κακήν τʼ ἐφράσσατο τέχνην.
lines.translit: steinomenē doliēn de kakēn t' ephrassato technēn

i18n.en: being straitened; and she devised a crafty and evil scheme.

lines.text: αἶψα δὲ ποιήσασα γένος πολιοῦ ἀδάμαντος
lines.translit: aipsa de poiēsasa genos poliou adamantos

i18n.en: And at once she made a stock of gray adamant,

lines.text: τεῦξε μέγα δρέπανον καὶ ἐπέφραδε παισὶ φίλοισιν·
lines.translit: teuxe mega drepanon kai epephrade paisi philoisin

i18n.en: and fashioned a great sickle, and told her dear children;

lines.text: εἶπε δὲ θαρσύνουσα, φίλον τετιημένη ἦτορ·
lines.translit: eipe de tharsynousa philon tetiēmenē ētor

i18n.en: and, grieved at heart, she spoke, encouraging them:

lines.text: παῖδες ἐμοὶ καὶ πατρὸς ἀτασθάλου, αἴ κʼ ἐθέλητε
lines.translit: paides emoi kai patros atasthalou ai k' ethelēte

i18n.en: “My children, and of a presumptuous father, if you are willing

lines.text: πείθεσθαι, πατρός κε κακὴν τισαίμεθα λώβην
lines.translit: peithesthai patros ke kakēn tisaimetha lōbēn

i18n.en: to obey, we might punish the evil outrage of your father;

lines.text: ὑμετέρου· πρότερος γὰρ ἀεικέα μήσατο ἔργα.
lines.translit: hymeterou proteros gar aeikea mēsato erga

i18n.en: for he was the first to devise shameful deeds.”

lines.text: ὣς φάτο· τοὺς δʼ ἄρα πάντας ἕλεν δέος, οὐδέ τις αὐτῶν
lines.translit: hōs phato tous d' ara pantas helen deos oude tis autōn

i18n.en: So she spoke; but fear seized them all, and none of them

lines.text: φθέγξατο. θαρσήσας δὲ μέγας Κρόνος ἀγκυλομήτης
lines.translit: phthenxato tharsēsas de megas Kronos ankylomētēs

i18n.en: uttered a sound. But great Kronos of the crooked counsel took courage,

lines.text: ἂψ αὖτις μύθοισι προσηύδα μητέρα κεδνήν·
lines.translit: aps autis mythoisi prosēuda mētera kednēn

i18n.en: and answered his dear mother again with words:

lines.text: μῆτερ, ἐγώ κεν τοῦτό γʼ ὑποσχόμενος τελέσαιμι
lines.translit: mēter egō ken touto g' hyposchomenos telesaimi

i18n.en: “Mother, I will promise and accomplish this

lines.text: ἔργον, ἐπεὶ πατρός γε δυσωνύμου οὐκ ἀλεγίζω
lines.translit: ergon epei patros ge dysōnymou ouk alegizō

i18n.en: deed, since I care nothing for our ill-named father;

lines.text: ἡμετέρου· πρότερος γὰρ ἀεικέα μήσατο ἔργα.
lines.translit: hēmeterou proteros gar aeikea mēsato erga

i18n.en: for he was the first to devise shameful deeds.”

lines.text: ὣς φάτο· γήθησεν δὲ μέγα φρεσὶ Γαῖα πελώρη·
lines.translit: hōs phato gēthēsen de mega phresi Gaia pelōrē

i18n.en: So he spoke; and huge Gaia rejoiced greatly in her heart;

lines.text: εἷσε δέ μιν κρύψασα λόχῳ· ἐνέθηκε δὲ χερσὶν
lines.translit: heise de min krypsasa lochō enethēke de chersin

i18n.en: and she set him in ambush, hiding him, and put into his hands

lines.text: ἅρπην καρχαρόδοντα· δόλον δʼ ὑπεθήκατο πάντα.
lines.translit: harpēn karcharodonta dolon d' hypethēkato panta

i18n.en: the jagged-toothed sickle, and told him all the trick.

lines.text: ἦλθε δὲ νύκτʼ ἐπάγων μέγας Οὐρανός, ἀμφὶ δὲ Γαίῃ
lines.translit: ēlthe de nykt' epagōn megas Ouranos amphi de Gaiē

i18n.en: And great Ouranos came, bringing on the night, and about Gaia

lines.text: ἱμείρων φιλότητος ἐπέσχετο καί ῥʼ ἐτανύσθη
lines.translit: himeirōn philotētos epescheto kai rh' etanysthē

i18n.en: he lay, desiring love, and spread himself out

lines.text: πάντη· ὃ δʼ ἐκ λοχέοιο πάις ὠρέξατο χειρὶ
lines.translit: pantē ho d' ek locheoio pais ōrexato cheiri

i18n.en: on every side; and the son reached out from the ambush with his

lines.text: σκαιῇ, δεξιτερῇ δὲ πελώριον ἔλλαβεν ἅρπην
lines.translit: skaiē dexiterē de pelōrion ellaben harpēn

i18n.en: left hand, and with his right he grasped the huge sickle,

lines.text: μακρὴν καρχαρόδοντα, φίλου δʼ ἀπὸ μήδεα πατρὸς
lines.translit: makrēn karcharodonta philou d' apo mēdea patros

i18n.en: long and jagged-toothed, and swiftly he reaped the genitals

lines.text: ἐσσυμένως ἤμησε, πάλιν δʼ ἔρριψε φέρεσθαι
lines.translit: essymenōs ēmēse palin d' erripse pheresthai

i18n.en: of his own father, and flung them back to be carried away

lines.text: ἐξοπίσω· τὰ μὲν οὔ τι ἐτώσια ἔκφυγε χειρός·
lines.translit: exopisō ta men ou ti etōsia ekphyge cheiros

i18n.en: behind him; and not in vain did they fly from his hand;

lines.text: ὅσσαι γὰρ ῥαθάμιγγες ἀπέσσυθεν αἱματόεσσαι,
lines.translit: hossai gar rhathaminges apessythen haimatoessai

i18n.en: for all the bloody drops that gushed forth,

lines.text: πάσας δέξατο Γαῖα· περιπλομένων δʼ ἐνιαυτῶν
lines.translit: pasas dexato Gaia periplomenōn d' eniautōn

i18n.en: Gaia received them all; and as the years rolled round

lines.text: γείνατʼ Ἐρινῦς τε κρατερὰς μεγάλους τε Γίγαντας,
lines.translit: geinat' Erinys te krateras megalous te Gigantas

i18n.en: she bore the strong Erinyes, and the great Giants,

notes.official: The Giants (*Γίγαντες*) are born here, earth-born from the blood-drops of the castrated Ouranos, together with the Erinyes and the ash-tree Nymphs (Meliai) — the Hesiodic Giants' aetiology. See on 50 for the distinction from the biblical/Enochic Nephilim and the shared Septuagint lexeme *γίγαντες*.

lines.text: τεύχεσι λαμπομένους, δολίχʼ ἔγχεα χερσὶν ἔχοντας,
lines.translit: teuchesi lampomenous dolich' enchea chersin echontas

i18n.en: gleaming in their armor, holding long spears in their hands,

lines.text: Νύμφας θʼ ἃς Μελίας καλέουσʼ ἐπʼ ἀπείρονα γαῖαν.
lines.translit: Nymphas th' has Melias kaleous' ep' apeirona gaian

i18n.en: and the Nymphs whom they call Meliai over the boundless earth.

lines.text: μήδεα δʼ ὡς τὸ πρῶτον ἀποτμήξας ἀδάμαντι
lines.translit: mēdea d' hōs to prōton apotmēxas adamanti

i18n.en: And the genitals, as soon as he had cut them off with the adamant

lines.text: κάββαλʼ ἀπʼ ἠπείροιο πολυκλύστῳ ἐνὶ πόντῳ,
lines.translit: kabbal' ap' ēpeiroio polyklystō eni pontō

i18n.en: and cast them from the land into the surging sea,

lines.text: ὣς φέρετʼ ἂμ πέλαγος πουλὺν χρόνον, ἀμφὶ δὲ λευκὸς
lines.translit: hōs pheret' am pelagos poulyn chronon amphi de leukos

i18n.en: were carried over the deep for a long time, and around them a white

lines.text: ἀφρὸς ἀπʼ ἀθανάτου χροὸς ὤρνυτο· τῷ δʼ ἔνι κούρη
lines.translit: aphros ap' athanatou chroos ōrnyto tō d' eni kourē

i18n.en: foam rose up from the immortal flesh; and within it a maiden

lines.text: ἐθρέφθη· πρῶτον δὲ Κυθήροισιν ζαθέοισιν
lines.translit: ethrephthē prōton de Kythēroisin zatheoisin

i18n.en: was nourished; first she drew near to holy Kythera,

lines.text: ἔπλητʼ, ἔνθεν ἔπειτα περίρρυτον ἵκετο Κύπρον.
lines.translit: eplēt' enthen epeita perirryton hiketo Kypron

i18n.en: and from there, afterward, she came to sea-girt Kypros.

lines.text: ἐκ δʼ ἔβη αἰδοίη καλὴ θεός, ἀμφὶ δὲ ποίη
lines.translit: ek d' ebē aidoiē kalē theos amphi de poiē

i18n.en: And there stepped forth a revered, beautiful goddess, and around her the grass

lines.text: ποσσὶν ὕπο ῥαδινοῖσιν ἀέξετο· τὴν δʼ Ἀφροδίτην
lines.translit: possin hypo rhadinoisin aexeto tēn d' Aphroditēn

i18n.en: grew up beneath her slender feet; and her Aphrodite,

lines.text: ἀφρογενέα τε θεὰν καὶ ἐυστέφανον Κυθέρειαν
lines.translit: aphrogenea te thean kai eustephanon Kythereian

i18n.en: the foam-born goddess, and well-crowned Kythereia,

notes.official: Line 196 is bracketed in the Perseus/Evelyn-White edition. It supplies the cult-titles 'foam-born goddess' and 'well-crowned Kythereia' that the following lines (197–198) then etymologize; some editors judge it an anticipatory gloss. It is retained and translated per project convention, the athetesis noted.

lines.text: κικλῄσκουσι θεοί τε καὶ ἀνέρες, οὕνεκʼ ἐν ἀφρῷ
lines.translit: kiklēskousi theoi te kai aneres hounek' en aphrō

i18n.en: gods and men call her, because in the foam

lines.text: θρέφθη· ἀτὰρ Κυθέρειαν, ὅτι προσέκυρσε Κυθήροις·
lines.translit: threphthē atar Kythereian hoti prosekyrse Kythērois

i18n.en: she was nourished; but Kythereia, because she came to Kythera;

lines.text: Κυπρογενέα δʼ, ὅτι γέντο πολυκλύστῳ ἐνὶ Κύπρῳ·
lines.translit: Kyprogenea d' hoti gento polyklystō eni Kyprō

i18n.en: and Kyprogenes, because she was born in surf-washed Kypros;

lines.text: ἠδὲ φιλομμηδέα, ὅτι μηδέων ἐξεφαάνθη.
lines.translit: ēde philommēdea hoti mēdeōn exephaanthē

i18n.en: and Philommedes, because she appeared out of the genitals.

lines.text: τῇ δʼ Ἔρος ὡμάρτησε καὶ Ἵμερος ἕσπετο καλὸς
lines.translit: tē d' Eros hōmartēse kai Himeros hespeto kalos

i18n.en: And Eros accompanied her, and fair Desire followed her,

notes.official: The Eros who here accompanies the new-born Aphrodite is the later, secondary Eros, distinct from the primordial cosmogonic Eros of 120; see there.

lines.text: γεινομένῃ τὰ πρῶτα θεῶν τʼ ἐς φῦλον ἰούσῃ.
lines.translit: geinomenē ta prōta theōn t' es phylon iousē

i18n.en: at her birth, and as she went into the tribe of the gods.

lines.text: ταύτην δʼ ἐξ ἀρχῆς τιμὴν ἔχει ἠδὲ λέλογχε
lines.translit: tautēn d' ex archēs timēn echei ēde lelonche

i18n.en: And from the beginning she has this honor, and has obtained

lines.text: μοῖραν ἐν ἀνθρώποισι καὶ ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσι,
lines.translit: moiran en anthrōpoisi kai athanatoisi theoisi

i18n.en: as her portion, among men and immortal gods,

lines.text: παρθενίους τʼ ὀάρους μειδήματά τʼ ἐξαπάτας τε
lines.translit: parthenious t' oarous meidēmata t' exapatas te

i18n.en: the whispers of girls, and smiles, and deceits,

lines.text: τέρψιν τε γλυκερὴν φιλότητά τε μειλιχίην τε.
lines.translit: terpsin te glykerēn philotēta te meilichiēn te

i18n.en: and sweet delight, and love, and tenderness.

lines.text: τοὺς δὲ πατὴρ Τιτῆνας ἐπίκλησιν καλέεσκε
lines.translit: tous de patēr Titēnas epiklēsin kaleeske

i18n.en: And these their father used to call by the surname of Titans,

notes.official: Lines 207–210 give Hesiod's own folk-etymology of the *Τιτῆνες* (Titans). Ouranos names his sons *Titēnas* while reproaching them, saying that 'straining' (*τιταίνοντας*, from *τιταίνω* 'to stretch, strain, overreach') in their presumption they had wrought a great deed, for which there would afterward be 'requital' (*τίσιν*, from *τίσις* 'retribution'). The passage turns on a double play — *τιταίνω* ~ *Τιτῆνες*, and the assonant *τίσις* — that cannot be carried into English; the translation renders *τιταίνοντας* 'straining' and *τίσιν* 'requital' literally, leaving the wordplay visible only in the Greek (Evelyn-White; West 1966). The etymology is Hesiod's invention: the true origin of the name *Τιτᾶνες* is unknown.

lines.text: παῖδας νεικείων μέγας Οὐρανός, οὓς τέκεν αὐτός·
lines.translit: paidas neikeiōn megas Ouranos hous teken autos

i18n.en: great Ouranos, reproaching the sons whom he himself had begotten;

lines.text: φάσκε δὲ τιταίνοντας ἀτασθαλίῃ μέγα ῥέξαι
lines.translit: phaske de titainontas atasthaliē mega rhexai

i18n.en: and he said that, straining in their presumption, they had wrought a great

notes.official: *τιταίνοντας* 'straining/overreaching' is the pun-word on which Hesiod's Titan-etymology turns; rendered literally so the wordplay stays visible in the Greek. See on 207.

lines.text: ἔργον, τοῖο δʼ ἔπειτα τίσιν μετόπισθεν ἔσεσθαι.
lines.translit: ergon toio d' epeita tisin metopisthen esesthai

i18n.en: deed, for which there would afterward be requital.

notes.official: *τίσιν* 'requital, retribution' is the second, assonant element of the wordplay (*τίσις*). See on 207.

lines.text: νὺξ δʼ ἔτεκεν στυγερόν τε Μόρον καὶ Κῆρα μέλαιναν
lines.translit: nyx d' eteken stygeron te Moron kai Kēra melainan

i18n.en: And Nyx bore hateful Doom, and black Fate,

notes.official: With Nyx's parthenogenetic brood (211–232) the poem turns from cosmic entities to *personified abstractions*: *Moros* 'Doom', *Kēr* 'Fate', *Thanatos* 'Death', *Hypnos* 'Sleep', the *Oneiroi* 'Dreams', and (from Eris, 226–232) *Ponos* 'Toil', *Limos* 'Famine', the *Machai* 'Battles', *Horkos* 'Oath', and the rest. Following Evelyn-White, and standard practice for this catalogue, the translation renders the transparent meanings of these abstractions and reserves transliteration for the more name-like or cult-established members — the Fates *Klōthō, Lachesis, Atropos* (218), *Nemesis* (223), and later Styx's children *Zēlos, Nikē, Kratos, Biē* (384–385). The Block A name-convention (transliterate personified cosmic theonyms) is thus not extended wholesale to the abstractions; the boundary is the one the reference edition itself draws.

lines.text: καὶ Θάνατον, τέκε δʼ Ὕπνον, ἔτικτε δὲ φῦλον Ὀνείρων·
lines.translit: kai Thanaton teke d' Hypnon etikte de phylon Oneirōn

i18n.en: and Death, and she bore Sleep, and she brought forth the tribe of Dreams.

lines.text: δεύτερον αὖ Μῶμον καὶ Ὀιζὺν ἀλγινόεσσαν
lines.translit: deuteron au Mōmon kai Oizyn alginoessan

i18n.en: And again, second, Blame, and painful Woe,

notes.official: Lines 213 and 214 are printed in the transposed order 214–213 (West 1966, adopted by the Perseus edition), so the *refId* sequence here is deliberately non-ascending; 213 (*'these dark Nyx bore, having lain with none'*) reads as a summarizing verse after the second instalment of the brood at 214. The transposition is editorial and text-critical, not a translation choice.

lines.text: οὔ τινι κοιμηθεῖσα θεὰ τέκε Νὺξ ἐρεβεννή,
lines.translit: ou tini koimētheisa thea teke Nyx erebennē

i18n.en: the goddess dark Nyx bore, having lain with none;

lines.text: Ἑσπερίδας θʼ, ᾗς μῆλα πέρην κλυτοῦ Ὠκεανοῖο
lines.translit: Hesperidas th' hēs mēla perēn klytou Ōkeanoio

i18n.en: and the Hesperides, for whom, beyond glorious Okeanos,

lines.text: χρύσεα καλὰ μέλουσι φέροντά τε δένδρεα καρπόν.
lines.translit: chrysea kala melousi pheronta te dendrea karpon

i18n.en: the fair golden apples are a care, and the trees that bear fruit.

lines.text: καὶ Μοίρας καὶ Κῆρας ἐγείνατο νηλεοποίνους,
lines.translit: kai Moiras kai Kēras egeinato nēleopoinous

i18n.en: And she bore the Destinies, and the ruthless-avenging Fates,

notes.official: *Μοίρας … Κῆρας* (217): Evelyn-White's distribution is retained — *Moirai* 'Destinies' and *Kēres* 'Fates' (the *νηλεοποίνους*, 'ruthless in requital'), with *Klōthō, Lachesis, Atropos* named in apposition at 218. The apportioning function ascribed to the Moirai here (giving mortals 'good and evil' at birth, 219) doublets their later birth from Zeus and Themis at 904–906 (Block D); the tension between the two Moirai-passages is a known feature of the poem and is left as transmitted.

lines.text: Κλωθώ τε Λάχεσίν τε καὶ Ἄτροπον, αἵτε βροτοῖσι
lines.translit: Klōthō te Lachesin te kai Atropon haite brotoisi

i18n.en: Klotho and Lachesis and Atropos, who to mortals

lines.text: γεινομένοισι διδοῦσιν ἔχειν ἀγαθόν τε κακόν τε,
lines.translit: geinomenoisi didousin echein agathon te kakon te

i18n.en: at their birth give both good and evil to have,

lines.text: αἵτʼ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε παραιβασίας ἐφέπουσιν·
lines.translit: hait' andrōn te theōn te paraibasias ephepousin

i18n.en: and who pursue the transgressions of men and of gods;

lines.text: οὐδέ ποτε λήγουσι θεαὶ δεινοῖο χόλοιο,
lines.translit: oude pote lēgousi theai deinoio choloio

i18n.en: and the goddesses never cease from their dread anger

lines.text: πρίν γʼ ἀπὸ τῷ δώωσι κακὴν ὄπιν, ὅς τις ἁμάρτῃ.
lines.translit: prin g' apo tō dōōsi kakēn opin hos tis hamartē

i18n.en: until they have given an evil requital to whoever transgresses.

lines.text: τίκτε δὲ καὶ Νέμεσιν, πῆμα θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσι,
lines.translit: tikte de kai Nemesin pēma thnētoisi brotoisi

i18n.en: And she bore Nemesis also, a bane to mortal men,

lines.text: Νὺξ ὀλοή· μετὰ τὴν δʼ Ἀπάτην τέκε καὶ Φιλότητα
lines.translit: Nyx oloē meta tēn d' Apatēn teke kai Philotēta

i18n.en: deadly Nyx; and after her she bore Deceit, and Friendship,

lines.text: Γῆράς τʼ οὐλόμενον, καὶ Ἔριν τέκε καρτερόθυμον.
lines.translit: Gēras t' oulomenon kai Erin teke karterothymon

i18n.en: and baneful Age, and she bore hard-hearted Strife.

lines.text: αὐτὰρ Ἔρις στυγερὴ τέκε μὲν Πόνον ἀλγινόεντα
lines.translit: autar Eris stygerē teke men Ponon alginoenta

i18n.en: But hateful Strife bore painful Toil,

lines.text: Λήθην τε Λιμόν τε καὶ Ἄλγεα δακρυόεντα
lines.translit: Lēthēn te Limon te kai Algea dakryoenta

i18n.en: and Forgetfulness, and Famine, and tearful Pains,

lines.text: Ὑσμίνας τε Μάχας τε Φόνους τʼ Ἀνδροκτασίας τε
lines.translit: Hysminas te Machas te Phonous t' Androktasias te

i18n.en: and Combats, and Battles, and Murders, and Slaughters of men,

lines.text: Νείκεά τε ψευδέας τε Λόγους Ἀμφιλλογίας τε
lines.translit: Neikea te pseudeas te Logous Amphillogias te

i18n.en: and Quarrels, and lying Words, and Disputes,

lines.text: Δυσνομίην τʼ Ἄτην τε, συνήθεας ἀλλήλῃσιν,
lines.translit: Dysnomiēn t' Atēn te synētheas allēlēsin

i18n.en: and Lawlessness and Ruin, close companions of one another,

lines.text: Ὅρκον θʼ, ὃς δὴ πλεῖστον ἐπιχθονίους ἀνθρώπους
lines.translit: Horkon th' hos dē pleiston epichthonious anthrōpous

i18n.en: and Oath, who most of all afflicts men upon the earth

notes.official: *Horkos* 'Oath' (231–232), last of Eris's children, is the personified oath that 'most of all afflicts men upon the earth whenever anyone willfully swears falsely' — the punitive numen of the perjured oath. He is to be kept distinct from the oath-by-Styx that Zeus institutes at 400 (*theōn megan horkon*, 'the great oath of the gods'), where *horkos* is the oath-object sworn *by*, not the avenging deity; see the note there.

lines.text: πημαίνει, ὅτε κέν τις ἑκὼν ἐπίορκον ὀμόσσῃ.
lines.translit: pēmainei hote ken tis hekōn epiorkon omossē

i18n.en: whenever anyone willfully swears a false oath.

lines.text: Νηρέα δʼ ἀψευδέα καὶ ἀληθέα γείνατο Πόντος,
lines.translit: Nērea d' apseudea kai alēthea geinato Pontos

i18n.en: And Pontos begot Nereus, without lie and truthful,

notes.official: *Pontos* (Sea) begets *Nereus*, the 'Old Man of the Sea' (234), characterized by a run of truth-words — *ἀψευδέα* 'without falsehood', *ἀληθέα* 'truthful' (233), *νημερτής* 'unerring' (235) — the same lexical field as the Muses' *pseudea/alēthea* declaration at 27–28. *Pontos* is kept personified (the sea-god, consort of Gaia) per the name convention; the truth-epithets are given their plain senses.

lines.text: πρεσβύτατον παίδων· αὐτὰρ καλέουσι γέροντα,
lines.translit: presbytaton paidōn autar kaleousi geronta

i18n.en: the eldest of his children; but they call him the Old Man,

lines.text: οὕνεκα νημερτής τε καὶ ἤπιος, οὐδὲ θεμιστέων
lines.translit: houneka nēmertēs te kai ēpios oude themisteōn

i18n.en: because he is unerring and kindly, and does not forget the ordinances,

lines.text: λήθεται, ἀλλὰ δίκαια καὶ ἤπια δήνεα οἶδεν·
lines.translit: lēthetai alla dikaia kai ēpia dēnea oiden

i18n.en: but knows just and kindly counsels;

lines.text: αὖτις δʼ αὖ Θαύμαντα μέγαν καὶ ἀγήνορα Φόρκυν
lines.translit: autis d' au Thaumanta megan kai agēnora Phorkyn

i18n.en: and again he begot great Thaumas, and proud Phorkys,

lines.text: Γαίῃ μισγόμενος καὶ Κητὼ καλλιπάρῃον
lines.translit: Gaiē misgomenos kai Kētō kalliparēon

i18n.en: mingling with Gaia, and fair-cheeked Keto,

lines.text: Εὐρυβίην τʼ ἀδάμαντος ἐνὶ φρεσὶ θυμὸν ἔχουσαν.
lines.translit: Eurybiēn t' adamantos eni phresi thymon echousan

i18n.en: and Eurybia, holding a spirit of adamant within her breast.

lines.text: Νηρῆος δʼ ἐγένοντο μεγήρατα τέκνα θεάων
lines.translit: Nērēos d' egenonto megērata tekna theaōn

i18n.en: And to Nereus were born much-loved children among the goddesses,

notes.official: The fifty Nereids (243–262) are transparent 'speaking-names' — *Plōtō* 'Sailer', *Galēnē* 'Calm', *Kymothoē* 'Wave-swift', *Pontoporeia* 'Sea-faring', *Nēmertēs* 'Unerring' — but, with Evelyn-White, the translation transliterates them as proper names rather than translating or glossing each sense; the catalogue is a litany of names, and rendering the meanings would turn a roll-call into a word-list. Where a name's sense is thematically pointed the note flags it (see 262).

lines.text: πόντῳ ἐν ἀτρυγέτῳ καὶ Δωρίδος ἠυκόμοιο,
lines.translit: pontō en atrygetō kai Dōridos ēukomoio

i18n.en: in the barren sea, and of rich-haired Doris,

lines.text: κούρης Ὠκεανοῖο, τελήεντος ποταμοῖο,
lines.translit: kourēs Ōkeanoio telēentos potamoio

i18n.en: daughter of Okeanos, the perfect river:

lines.text: Πλωτώ τʼ Εὐκράντη τε Σαώ τʼ Ἀμφιτρίτη τε
lines.translit: Plōtō t' Eukrantē te Saō t' Amphitritē te

i18n.en: Ploto, and Eukrante, and Sao, and Amphitrite,

lines.text: Εὐδώρη τε Θέτις τε Γαλήνη τε Γλαύκη τε
lines.translit: Eudōrē te Thetis te Galēnē te Glaukē te

i18n.en: and Eudora, and Thetis, and Galene, and Glauke,

lines.text: Κυμοθόη Σπειώ τε Θόη θʼ Ἀλίη τʼ ἐρόεσσα
lines.translit: Kymothoē Speiō te Thoē th' Aliē t' eroessa

i18n.en: Kymothoe, and Speio, and Thoe, and lovely Halie,

lines.text: Πασιθέη τʼ Ἐρατώ τε καὶ Εὐνίκη ῥοδόπηχυς
lines.translit: Pasitheē t' Eratō te kai Eunikē rhodopēchys

i18n.en: and Pasithea, and Erato, and Eunike of the rosy arms,

lines.text: καὶ Μελίτη χαρίεσσα καὶ Εὐλιμένη καὶ Ἀγαυὴ
lines.translit: kai Melitē chariessa kai Eulimenē kai Agauē

i18n.en: and graceful Melite, and Eulimene, and Agaue,

lines.text: Δωτώ τε Πρωτώ τε Φέρουσά τε Δυναμένη τε
lines.translit: Dōtō te Prōtō te Pherousa te Dynamenē te

i18n.en: and Doto, and Proto, and Pherusa, and Dynamene,

lines.text: Νησαίη τε καὶ Ἀκταίη καὶ Πρωτομέδεια
lines.translit: Nēsaiē te kai Aktaiē kai Prōtomedeia

i18n.en: and Nesaie, and Aktaie, and Protomedeia,

lines.text: Δωρὶς καὶ Πανόπεια καὶ εὐειδὴς Γαλάτεια
lines.translit: Dōris kai Panopeia kai eueidēs Galateia

i18n.en: Doris, and Panopeia, and shapely Galateia,

lines.text: Ἱπποθόη τʼ ἐρόεσσα καὶ Ἱππονόη ῥοδόπηχυς
lines.translit: Hippothoē t' eroessa kai Hipponoē rhodopēchys

i18n.en: and lovely Hippothoe, and Hipponoe of the rosy arms,

lines.text: Κυμοδόκη θʼ, ἣ κύματʼ ἐν ἠεροειδέι πόντῳ
lines.translit: Kymodokē th' hē kymat' en ēeroeidei pontō

i18n.en: and Kymodoke, who the waves on the misty sea,

lines.text: πνοιάς τε ζαέων ἀνέμων σὺν Κυματολήγῃ
lines.translit: pnoias te zaeōn anemōn syn Kymatolēgē

i18n.en: and the blasts of stormy winds, together with Kymatolege,

lines.text: ῥεῖα πρηΰνει καὶ ἐυσφύρῳ Ἀμφιτρίτῃ,
lines.translit: rheia prēynei kai eusphyrō Amphitritē

i18n.en: readily calms, and with fair-ankled Amphitrite,

lines.text: Κυμώ τʼ Ἠιόνη τε ἐυστέφανός θʼ Ἁλιμήδη
lines.translit: Kymō t' Ēionē te eustephanos th' Halimēdē

i18n.en: and Kymo, and Eione, and fair-crowned Halimede,

lines.text: Γλαυκονόμη τε φιλομμειδὴς καὶ Ποντοπόρεια
lines.translit: Glaukonomē te philommeidēs kai Pontoporeia

i18n.en: and laughter-loving Glaukonome, and Pontoporeia,

lines.text: Ληαγόρη τε καὶ Εὐαγόρη καὶ Λαομέδεια
lines.translit: Lēagorē te kai Euagorē kai Laomedeia

i18n.en: and Leagore, and Euagore, and Laomedeia,

lines.text: Πουλυνόη τε καὶ Αὐτονόη καὶ Λυσιάνασσα
lines.translit: Poulynoē te kai Autonoē kai Lysianassa

i18n.en: and Poulynoe, and Autonoe, and Lysianassa,

lines.text: Εὐάρνη τε φυήν τʼ ἐρατὴ καὶ εἶδος ἄμωμος
lines.translit: Euarnē te phyēn t' eratē kai eidos amōmos

i18n.en: and Euarne, lovely in stature and flawless in form,

lines.text: καὶ Ψαμάθη χαρίεσσα δέμας δίη τε Μενίππη
lines.translit: kai Psamathē chariessa demas diē te Menippē

i18n.en: and graceful Psamathe, comely of body, and divine Menippe,

lines.text: Νησώ τʼ Εὐπόμπη τε Θεμιστώ τε Προνόη τε
lines.translit: Nēsō t' Eupompē te Themistō te Pronoē te

i18n.en: Neso, and Eupompe, and Themisto, and Pronoe,

lines.text: Νημερτής θʼ, ἣ πατρὸς ἔχει νόον ἀθανάτοιο.
lines.translit: Nēmertēs th' hē patros echei noon athanatoio

i18n.en: and Nemertes, who has the mind of her immortal father.

notes.official: The Nereid catalogue closes on *Nēmertēs* 'Unerring' (262), 'who has the mind of her immortal father' — the daughter whose name reprises Nereus's own defining epithet *νημερτής* (235). The transliteration is kept (per 240), the point of the name carried in this note.

lines.text: αὗται μὲν Νηρῆος ἀμύμονος ἐξεγένοντο
lines.translit: hautai men Nērēos amymonos exegenonto

i18n.en: These were born of blameless Nereus,

lines.text: κοῦραι πεντήκοντα, ἀμύμονα ἔργα ἰδυῖαι.
lines.translit: kourai pentēkonta amymona erga idyiai

i18n.en: fifty maidens, skilled in blameless works.

lines.text: Θαύμας δʼ Ὠκεανοῖο βαθυρρείταο θύγατρα
lines.translit: Thaumas d' Ōkeanoio bathyrreitao thygatra

i18n.en: And Thaumas wedded Elektra, the daughter of deep-flowing Okeanos;

lines.text: ἠγάγετʼ Ἠλέκτρην· ἣ δʼ ὠκεῖαν τέκεν Ἶριν
lines.translit: ēgaget' Ēlektrēn hē d' ōkeian teken Irin

i18n.en: and she bore swift Iris,

lines.text: ἠυκόμους θʼ Ἁρπυίας Ἀελλώ τʼ Ὠκυπέτην τε,
lines.translit: ēukomous th' Harpyias Aellō t' Ōkypetēn te

i18n.en: and the fair-haired Harpies, Aello and Okypete,

lines.text: αἵ ῥʼ ἀνέμων πνοιῇσι καὶ οἰωνοῖς ἅμʼ ἕπονται
lines.translit: hai rh' anemōn pnoiēsi kai oiōnois ham' hepontai

i18n.en: who keep pace with the blasts of the winds and with the birds

lines.text: ὠκείῃς πτερύγεσσι· μεταχρόνιαι γὰρ ἴαλλον.
lines.translit: ōkeiēs pterygessi metachroniai gar iallon

i18n.en: on their swift wings; for they dart aloft in the air.

lines.text: Φόρκυϊ δʼ αὖ Κητὼ Γραίας τέκε καλλιπαρῄους
lines.translit: Phorkyi d' au Kētō Graias teke kalliparēous

i18n.en: And again, to Phorkys Keto bore the fair-cheeked Graiai,

notes.official: *Graiai* (270–272), daughters of Phorkys and Keto, are 'grey (*poliai*) from birth' (271) — Hesiod's transparent folk-etymology of the name (*Graiai* ~ *graus* 'old woman', *poliai* 'grey'). Following the Greek-form name convention the translation transliterates 'Graiai' (not the Latinized 'Graeae') and renders the etymologizing epithet literally ('grey from their birth'), leaving the *Graiai* ~ 'grey' play visible only in the Greek, as with the Titan etymology at 207–210.

lines.text: ἐκ γενετῆς πολιάς, τὰς δὴ Γραίας καλέουσιν
lines.translit: ek genetēs polias tas dē Graias kaleousin

i18n.en: grey from their birth—whom indeed both the immortal gods

lines.text: ἀθάνατοί τε θεοὶ χαμαὶ ἐρχόμενοί τʼ ἄνθρωποι,
lines.translit: athanatoi te theoi chamai erchomenoi t' anthrōpoi

i18n.en: and men who walk upon the earth call the Graiai:

lines.text: Πεμφρηδώ τʼ ἐύπεπλον Ἐνυώ τε κροκόπεπλον,
lines.translit: Pemphrēdō t' eupeplon Enyō te krokopeplon

i18n.en: Pemphredo well-clad, and saffron-robed Enyo,

lines.text: Γοργούς θʼ, αἳ ναίουσι πέρην κλυτοῦ Ὠκεανοῖο
lines.translit: Gorgous th' hai naiousi perēn klytou Ōkeanoio

i18n.en: and the Gorgons, who dwell beyond glorious Okeanos

lines.text: ἐσχατιῇ πρὸς Νυκτός, ἵνʼ Ἑσπερίδες λιγύφωνοι,
lines.translit: eschatiē pros Nyktos hin' Hesperides ligyphōnoi

i18n.en: at the edge, toward Night, where the clear-voiced Hesperides are:

lines.text: Σθεννώ τʼ Εὐρυάλη τε Μέδουσά τε λυγρὰ παθοῦσα.
lines.translit: Sthennō t' Euryalē te Medousa te lygra pathousa

i18n.en: Sthenno, and Euryale, and Medousa, who suffered a woeful fate.

lines.text: ἣ μὲν ἔην θνητή, αἳ δʼ ἀθάνατοι καὶ ἀγήρῳ,
lines.translit: hē men eēn thnētē hai d' athanatoi kai agērō

i18n.en: She was mortal, but the two were deathless and unaging,

lines.text: αἱ δύο· τῇ δὲ μιῇ παρελέξατο Κυανοχαίτης
lines.translit: hai dyo tē de miē parelexato Kyanochaitēs

i18n.en: the two of them; and with the one the Dark-haired One lay

lines.text: ἐν μαλακῷ λειμῶνι καὶ ἄνθεσιν εἰαρινοῖσιν.
lines.translit: en malakō leimōni kai anthesin eiarinoisin

i18n.en: in a soft meadow among the spring flowers.

lines.text: τῆς δʼ ὅτε δὴ Περσεὺς κεφαλὴν ἀπεδειροτόμησεν,
lines.translit: tēs d' hote dē Perseus kephalēn apedeirotomēsen

i18n.en: And when Perseus cut off her head from her neck,

lines.text: ἔκθορε Χρυσαωρ τε μέγας καὶ Πήγασος ἵππος.
lines.translit: ekthore Chrysaōr te megas kai Pēgasos hippos

i18n.en: there sprang forth great Chrysaor and the horse Pegasos.

notes.official: Source-orthography note: the Perseus text reads *Χρυσαωρ* here without its final accent (contrast the correctly accented *Χρυσάωρ* at 287); the source *text* field preserves the edition verbatim and is not silently corrected, while the transliteration and translation give the standard 'Chrysaor'. On the births of *Chrysaor* and *Pegasos* from the severed neck of Medusa, and their etymologies, see 282–283.

lines.text: τῷ μὲν ἐπώνυμον ἦεν, ὅτʼ Ὠκεανοῦ περὶ πηγὰς
lines.translit: tō men epōnymon ēen hot' Ōkeanou peri pēgas

i18n.en: To him the name came because he was born beside the springs of Okeanos,

notes.official: *Pēgasos* is etymologized at 282 from the *pēgai* 'springs' of Okeanos beside which he was born (*ὅτʼ Ὠκεανοῦ περὶ πηγὰς γένθʼ*). With the Titan (207–210) and Graiai (270–271) etymologies, the pun is rendered by translating the explanatory clause literally ('because he was born beside the springs of Okeanos') and leaving the *Pēgasos* ~ *pēgai* assonance audible only in the Greek; no English pun is manufactured and no inline gloss is added.

lines.text: γένθʼ, ὃ δʼ ἄορ χρύσειον ἔχων μετὰ χερσὶ φίλῃσιν.
lines.translit: genth' ho d' aor chryseion echōn meta chersi philēsin

i18n.en: while the other held a golden blade in his dear hands.

notes.official: *Chrysaōr* is etymologized at 283 from the *ἄορ χρύσειον* 'golden blade' he holds at birth (*chrys-* 'gold' + *aōr* 'sword'). As at 282, the clause is rendered literally and the name-play is left in the Greek.

lines.text: χὠ μὲν ἀποπτάμενος προλιπὼν χθόνα, μητέρα μήλων,
lines.translit: chō men apoptamenos prolipōn chthona mētera mēlōn

i18n.en: And Pegasos, flying away and leaving the earth, the mother of flocks,

lines.text: ἵκετʼ ἐς ἀθανάτους· Ζηνὸς δʼ ἐν δώμασι ναίει
lines.translit: hiket' es athanatous Zēnos d' en dōmasi naiei

i18n.en: came to the immortals; and he dwells in the house of Zeus,

lines.text: βροντήν τε στεροπήν τε φέρων Διὶ μητιόεντι.
lines.translit: brontēn te steropēn te pherōn Dii mētioenti

i18n.en: bearing thunder and lightning to wise Zeus.

lines.text: Χρυσάωρ δʼ ἔτεκεν τρικέφαλον Γηρυονῆα
lines.translit: Chrysaōr d' eteken trikephalon Gēryonēa

i18n.en: And Chrysaor begot three-headed Geryones,

lines.text: μιχθεὶς Καλλιρόῃ κούρῃ κλυτοῦ Ὠκεανοῖο.
lines.translit: michtheis Kalliroē kourē klytou Ōkeanoio

i18n.en: having mingled with Kalliroe, daughter of glorious Okeanos.

lines.text: τὸν μὲν ἄρʼ ἐξενάριξε βίη Ἡρακληείη
lines.translit: ton men ar' exenarixe biē Hēraklēeiē

i18n.en: Him the might of Herakles slew,

lines.text: βουσὶ παρʼ εἰλιπόδεσσι περιρρύτῳ εἰν Ἐρυθείῃ
lines.translit: bousi par' eilipodessi perirrytō ein Erytheiē

i18n.en: beside his shambling cattle in sea-girt Erytheia,

lines.text: ἤματι τῷ ὅτε περ βοῦς ἤλασεν εὐρυμετώπους
lines.translit: ēmati tō hote per bous ēlasen eurymetōpous

i18n.en: on that day when he drove the broad-browed cattle

lines.text: Τίρυνθʼ εἰς ἱερὴν διαβὰς πόρον Ὠκεανοῖο
lines.translit: Tirynth' eis hierēn diabas poron Ōkeanoio

i18n.en: to holy Tiryns, crossing the ford of Okeanos,

lines.text: Ὄρθον τε κτείνας καὶ βουκόλον Εὐρυτίωνα
lines.translit: Orthon te kteinas kai boukolon Eurytiōna

i18n.en: and having slain Orthos and the herdsman Eurytion

lines.text: σταθμῷ ἐν ἠερόεντι πέρην κλυτοῦ Ὠκεανοῖο.
lines.translit: stathmō en ēeroenti perēn klytou Ōkeanoio

i18n.en: in the misty steading beyond glorious Okeanos.

lines.text: ἣ δʼ ἔτεκʼ ἄλλο πέλωρον ἀμήχανον, οὐδὲν ἐοικὸς
lines.translit: hē d' etek' allo pelōron amēchanon ouden eoikos

i18n.en: And she bore yet another monster, resistless, like neither

notes.official: The mother of the monster Echidna (295–305) is left implicit in the Greek: *ἣ δʼ ἔτεκʼ* 'and she bore'. The nearest grammatical antecedent is Kalliroe (288), but the mythographic logic of the passage — and the summarizing line 'this is the race sprung from Keto and Phorkys' (336) — has led Evelyn-White and most editors to supply Keto. The translation keeps the bare 'she' and follows the Keto reading in sense; the ambiguity is genuine and is noted, not silently resolved.

lines.text: θνητοῖς ἀνθρώποις οὐδʼ ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσιν,
lines.translit: thnētois anthrōpois oud' athanatoisi theoisin

i18n.en: to mortal men nor to the immortal gods,

lines.text: σπῆι ἔνι γλαφυρῷ θείην κρατερόφρονʼ Ἔχιδναν,
lines.translit: spēi eni glaphyrō theiēn kraterophron' Echidnan

i18n.en: in a hollow cave: divine, strong-hearted Echidna,

lines.text: ἥμισυ μὲν νύμφην ἑλικώπιδα καλλιπάρῃον,
lines.translit: hēmisy men nymphēn helikōpida kalliparēon

i18n.en: half a quick-glancing, fair-cheeked nymph,

lines.text: ἥμισυ δʼ αὖτε πέλωρον ὄφιν δεινόν τε μέγαν τε
lines.translit: hēmisy d' aute pelōron ophin deinon te megan te

i18n.en: but half again a monstrous serpent, terrible and great,

notes.official: Echidna is 'half a *nymphē*' (298) and 'half a monstrous *ophis*' (299). Greek *ophis* 'serpent' (299, 334) and *drakōn* 'serpent, dragon' (322–323) are largely synonymous in early epic; with Evelyn-White the translation renders *ophis* 'serpent' and *drakōn* 'dragon' as the context of each line invites, without imposing a fixed technical distinction the Greek does not mark. *Nymphē* is kept as 'nymph' (its plain sense, a minor female divinity), here of the maiden-and-serpent hybrid; the same word recurs of Echidna at 305.

lines.text: αἰόλον ὠμηστὴν ζαθέης ὑπὸ κεύθεσι γαίης.
lines.translit: aiolon ōmēstēn zatheēs hypo keuthesi gaiēs

i18n.en: gleaming and flesh-eating, beneath the hidden places of the holy earth.

lines.text: ἔνθα δέ οἱ σπέος ἐστὶ κάτω κοίλῃ ὑπὸ πέτρῃ
lines.translit: entha de hoi speos esti katō koilē hypo petrē

i18n.en: There she has a cave below, under a hollow rock,

lines.text: τηλοῦ ἀπʼ ἀθανάτων τε θεῶν θνητῶν τʼ ἀνθρώπων·
lines.translit: tēlou ap' athanatōn te theōn thnētōn t' anthrōpōn

i18n.en: far from the immortal gods and from mortal men;

lines.text: ἔνθʼ ἄρα οἱ δάσσαντο θεοὶ κλυτὰ δώματα ναίειν.
lines.translit: enth' ara hoi dassanto theoi klyta dōmata naiein

i18n.en: there the gods allotted her glorious halls to dwell in.

lines.text: ἣ δʼ ἔρυτʼ εἰν Ἀρίμοισιν ὑπὸ χθονὶ λυγρὴ Ἔχιδνα,
lines.translit: hē d' eryt' ein Arimoisin hypo chthoni lygrē Echidna

i18n.en: And there, among the Arimoi, she lurked beneath the earth, baneful Echidna,

notes.official: *εἰν Ἀρίμοισιν* (304; cf. *Iliad* 2.783) is an ancient crux. Read as a dative plural of a people, it means 'among the Arimoi'; read as *ein Arimois*, a place, 'in Arima' — a district variously located in Cilicia, Lydia, or Mysia already in antiquity (cf. Strabo 13.4.6). The translation commits to the people-reading, 'among the Arimoi', a small refinement away from Evelyn-White's place-leaning 'in the land of the Arimi'; the alternative is recorded here, and the referent's location, unrecoverable, is left unglossed.

lines.text: ἀθάνατος νύμφη καὶ ἀγήραος ἤματα πάντα.
lines.translit: athanatos nymphē kai agēraos ēmata panta

i18n.en: a deathless nymph and unaging all her days.

lines.text: τῇ δὲ Τυφάονά φασι μιγήμεναι ἐν φιλότητι
lines.translit: tē de Typhaona phasi migēmenai en philotēti

i18n.en: With her they say Typhaon mingled in love,

lines.text: δεινόν θʼ ὑβριστήν τʼ ἄνομόν θʼ ἑλικώπιδι κούρῃ·
lines.translit: deinon th' hybristēn t' anomon th' helikōpidi kourē

i18n.en: the terrible, violent, lawless one, with the quick-glancing maiden;

lines.text: ἣ δʼ ὑποκυσαμένη τέκετο κρατερόφρονα τέκνα.
lines.translit: hē d' hypokysamenē teketo kraterophrona tekna

i18n.en: and she conceived and bore strong-hearted children.

lines.text: Ὄρθον μὲν πρῶτον κύνα γείνατο Γηρυονῆι·
lines.translit: Orthon men prōton kyna geinato Gēryonēi

i18n.en: First she bore Orthos, the hound of Geryones;

lines.text: δεύτερον αὖτις ἔτικτεν ἀμήχανον, οὔ τι φατειὸν
lines.translit: deuteron autis etikten amēchanon ou ti phateion

i18n.en: second, again, she brought forth one resistless, not to be named,

lines.text: Κέρβερον ὠμηστήν, Ἀίδεω κύνα χαλκεόφωνον,
lines.translit: Kerberon ōmēstēn Aideō kyna chalkeophōnon

i18n.en: Kerberos the flesh-eater, the brazen-voiced hound of Hades,

lines.text: πεντηκοντακέφαλον, ἀναιδέα τε κρατερόν τε·
lines.translit: pentēkontakephalon anaidea te krateron te

i18n.en: fifty-headed, shameless and strong;

lines.text: τὸ τρίτον Ὕδρην αὖτις ἐγείνατο λυγρὰ ἰδυῖαν
lines.translit: to triton Hydrēn autis egeinato lygra idyian

i18n.en: third, again, she bore the baleful-minded Hydra

lines.text: Λερναίην, ἣν θρέψε θεὰ λευκώλενος Ἥρη
lines.translit: Lernaiēn hēn threpse thea leukōlenos Hērē

i18n.en: of Lerna, whom the goddess white-armed Hera reared,

lines.text: ἄπλητον κοτέουσα βίῃ Ἡρακληείῃ.
lines.translit: aplēton koteousa biē Hēraklēeiē

i18n.en: boundlessly wroth against the might of Herakles.

lines.text: καὶ τὴν μὲν Διὸς υἱὸς ἐνήρατο νηλέι χαλκῷ
lines.translit: kai tēn men Dios hyios enērato nēlei chalkō

i18n.en: And her the son of Zeus slew with the pitiless bronze,

lines.text: Ἀμφιτρυωνιάδης σὺν ἀρηιφίλῳ Ἰολάῳ
lines.translit: Amphitryōniadēs syn arēiphilō Iolaō

i18n.en: the son of Amphitryon, with war-loving Iolaos,

lines.text: Ηρακλέης βουλῇσιν Ἀθηναίης ἀγελείης.
lines.translit: Ērakleēs boulēsin Athēnaiēs ageleiēs

i18n.en: Herakles, by the counsels of Athena, driver of the spoil.

lines.text: ἣ δὲ Χίμαιραν ἔτικτε πνέουσαν ἀμαιμάκετον πῦρ,
lines.translit: hē de Chimairan etikte pneousan amaimaketon pyr

i18n.en: And she bore Chimaira, who breathed raging fire,

notes.official: *Chimaira* (319), the fire-breathing monster, bears a name that is also the common noun *chimaira* 'she-goat' — which names her middle head (*μέσση δὲ χίμαιρα*, 323). As with the *gaia/ouranos* boundary in Block A, the translation fixes the personified/common-noun line where Evelyn-White does: 'Chimaira' the monster (capitalized, Greek form, not Latinized 'Chimaera'), 'she-goat' the common noun of the head (322–323). The name's transparency — a monster literally part she-goat — is thus visible without capitalizing the animal.

lines.text: δεινήν τε μεγάλην τε ποδώκεά τε κρατερήν τε·
lines.translit: deinēn te megalēn te podōkea te kraterēn te

i18n.en: terrible and great and swift-footed and strong;

lines.text: τῆς δʼ ἦν τρεῖς κεφαλαί· μία μὲν χαροποῖο λέοντος,
lines.translit: tēs d' ēn treis kephalai mia men charopoio leontos

i18n.en: she had three heads: one of a fierce-eyed lion,

lines.text: ἣ δὲ χιμαίρης, ἣ δʼ ὄφιος, κρατεροῖο δράκοντος,
lines.translit: hē de chimairēs hē d' ophios krateroio drakontos

i18n.en: another of a she-goat, another of a serpent, a mighty dragon;

lines.text: πρόσθε λέων, ὄπιθεν δὲ δράκων, μέσση δὲ χίμαιρα,
lines.translit: prosthe leōn opithen de drakōn messē de chimaira

i18n.en: in front a lion, behind a dragon, in the middle a she-goat,

notes.official: Lines 323–324 are bracketed (athetized) in the Perseus/Evelyn-White edition as a likely elaboration of the Chimaira's description (they partly restate 321–322 and 319); per project convention the transmitted lines are retained and translated, the athetesis recorded here rather than in the surface. On *χίμαιρα* 'she-goat' as the common noun naming the middle head, see 319.

lines.text: δεινὸν ἀποπνείουσα πυρὸς μένος αἰθομένοιο.
lines.translit: deinon apopneiousa pyros menos aithomenoio

i18n.en: breathing forth the terrible strength of blazing fire.

notes.official: See on 323: this line falls within the athetized 323–324 and is retained and translated per convention.

lines.text: τὴν μὲν Πήγασος εἷλε καὶ ἐσθλὸς Βελλεροφόντης.
lines.translit: tēn men Pēgasos heile kai esthlos Bellerophontēs

i18n.en: Her Pegasos and noble Bellerophontes slew.

lines.text: ἣ δʼ ἄρα Φῖκʼ ὀλοὴν τέκε Καδμείοισιν ὄλεθρον
lines.translit: hē d' ara Phik' oloēn teke Kadmeioisin olethron

i18n.en: And she bore the deadly Sphinx, a ruin for the Kadmeans,

notes.official: The source reads *Φῖκʼ* — *Phix*, the Boeotian dialect form (from Mt. Phíkion) that Hesiod, a Boeotian poet, uses for the creature panhellenically called the *Sphinx* (*Σφίγξ*). The translation gives the familiar panhellenic Greek name 'Sphinx' (itself Greek, not a Latinization, and the form the reader will recognize), recording the Boeotian *Phix* that the source preserves here. The mother of the Sphinx and the Nemean lion is grammatically ambiguous: 'she' (326) is read by Evelyn-White as the just-named Chimaira, but many editors (West 1966) take it as Echidna resumed, mated with her own son Orthos (327); the bare 'she' preserves the ambiguity.

lines.text: Ὅρθῳ ὑποδμηθεῖσα Νεμειαῖόν τε λέοντα,
lines.translit: Horthō hypodmētheisa Nemeiaion te leonta

i18n.en: subdued by Orthos, and the Nemean lion,

lines.text: τόν ῥʼ Ἥρη θρέψασα Διὸς κυδρὴ παράκοιτις
lines.translit: ton rh' Hērē threpsasa Dios kydrē parakoitis

i18n.en: which Hera, the glorious consort of Zeus, reared

lines.text: γουνοῖσιν κατένασσε Νεμείης, πῆμʼ ἀνθρώποις.
lines.translit: gounoisin katenasse Nemeiēs pēm' anthrōpois

i18n.en: and settled among the hills of Nemea, a bane to men.

lines.text: ἔνθʼ ἄρʼ ὃ οἰκείων ἐλεφαίρετο φῦλʼ ἀνθρώπων,
lines.translit: enth' ar' ho oikeiōn elephaireto phyl' anthrōpōn

i18n.en: There it preyed upon the tribes of men who dwelt about,

lines.text: κοιρανέων Τρητοῖο Νεμείης ἠδʼ Ἀπέσαντος·
lines.translit: koiraneōn Trētoio Nemeiēs ēd' Apesantos

i18n.en: lording it over Tretos of Nemea and Apesas;

lines.text: ἀλλά ἑ ἲς ἐδάμασσε βίης Ἡρακληείης.
lines.translit: alla he is edamasse biēs Hēraklēeiēs

i18n.en: but the strength of the might of Herakles subdued it.

lines.text: Κητὼ δʼ ὁπλότατον Φόρκυι φιλότητι μιγεῖσα
lines.translit: Kētō d' hoplotaton Phorkyi philotēti migeisa

i18n.en: And Keto, mingling in love with Phorkys, as her youngest

lines.text: γείνατο δεινὸν ὄφιν, ὃς ἐρεμνῆς κεύθεσι γαίης
lines.translit: geinato deinon ophin hos eremnēs keuthesi gaiēs

i18n.en: bore a terrible serpent, who in the hidden places of the dark earth,

lines.text: πείρασιν ἐν μεγάλοις παγχρύσεα μῆλα φυλάσσει.
lines.translit: peirasin en megalois panchrysea mēla phylassei

i18n.en: at the great bounds, guards the all-golden apples.

lines.text: τοῦτο μὲν ἐκ Κητοῦς καὶ Φόρκυνος γένος ἐστίν.
lines.translit: touto men ek Kētous kai Phorkynos genos estin

i18n.en: This is the race sprung from Keto and Phorkys.

lines.text: Τηθὺς δʼ Ὠκεανῷ Ποταμοὺς τέκε δινήεντας,
lines.translit: Tēthys d' Ōkeanō Potamous teke dinēentas

i18n.en: And Tethys bore to Okeanos the eddying Rivers:

lines.text: Νεῖλόν τʼ Ἀλφειόν τε καὶ Ἠριδανὸν βαθυδίνην
lines.translit: Neilon t' Alpheion te kai Ēridanon bathydinēn

i18n.en: Neilos, and Alpheios, and deep-eddying Eridanos,

notes.official: The river-catalogue (338–345) is given in Greek transliteration throughout — *Neilos, Alpheios, Istros, Maiandros, Skamandros* — per the Block A name convention (Greek forms, not Latinized), here applied even to streams carrying entrenched English exonyms: *Neilos* (not 'Nile'), *Istros* (the Greek name of the lower Danube, not 'Danube'), *Maiandros* (not 'Maeander'), *Skamandros* (not 'Scamander'). Evelyn-White's Latinized forms (Nilus, Ister, Maeander, Scamander) are declined; the trade-off with reader-familiarity is flagged for review.

lines.text: Στρυμόνα Μαίανδρόν τε καὶ Ἴστρον καλλιρέεθρον
lines.translit: Strymona Maiandron te kai Istron kallireethron

i18n.en: Strymon, and Maiandros, and fair-flowing Istros,

lines.text: Φᾶσίν τε Ῥῆσόν τʼ Ἀχελώιόν τʼ ἀργυροδίνην
lines.translit: Phasin te Rhēson t' Achelōion t' argyrodinēn

i18n.en: Phasis, and Rhesos, and silver-eddying Acheloios,

lines.text: Νέσσον τε Ῥοδίον θʼ Ἁλιάκμονά θʼ Ἑπτάπορόν τε
lines.translit: Nesson te Rhodion th' Haliakmona th' Heptaporon te

i18n.en: Nessos, and Rhodios, and Haliakmon, and Heptaporos,

lines.text: Γρήνικόν τε καὶ Αἴσηπον θεῖόν τε Σιμοῦντα
lines.translit: Grēnikon te kai Aisēpon theion te Simounta

i18n.en: Granikos, and Aisepos, and divine Simoeis,

notes.official: Source-orthography note: the edition reads *Γρήνικόν* (with eta) at 342; the translation gives the standard river-name 'Granikos' (*Γράνικος*), normalizing the vowel as the name convention normalizes other variant spellings. The transliteration field follows the source (*Grēnikon*).

lines.text: Πηνειόν τε καὶ Ἕρμον ἐυρρείτην τε Κάικον
lines.translit: Pēneion te kai Hermon eurreitēn te Kaikon

i18n.en: Peneios, and Hermos, and fair-flowing Kaikos,

lines.text: Σαγγάριόν τε μέγαν Λάδωνά τε Παρθένιόν τε
lines.translit: Sangarion te megan Ladōna te Parthenion te

i18n.en: and great Sangarios, and Ladon, and Parthenios,

lines.text: Εὔηνόν τε καὶ Ἄρδησκον θεῖόν τε Σκάμανδρον.
lines.translit: Euēnon te kai Ardēskon theion te Skamandron

i18n.en: and Euenos, and Ardeskos, and divine Skamandros.

lines.text: τίκτε δὲ θυγατέρων ἱερὸν γένος, αἳ κατὰ γαῖαν
lines.translit: tikte de thygaterōn hieron genos hai kata gaian

i18n.en: And she bore a holy race of daughters, who over the earth,

lines.text: ἄνδρας κουρίζουσι σὺν Ἀπόλλωνι ἄνακτι
lines.translit: andras kourizousi syn Apollōni anakti

i18n.en: rear men to manhood, together with lord Apollo

notes.official: The river-daughters (346–348) *ἄνδρας κουρίζουσι* 'rear men to manhood' together with Apollo and the Rivers — the nurturing-of-youth motif (*kour-*) that recurs as Hekate's *kourotrophos* title at 450. Rendered 'rear men to manhood' with Evelyn-White.

lines.text: καὶ Ποταμοῖς, ταύτην δὲ Διὸς πάρα μοῖραν ἔχουσι,
lines.translit: kai Potamois tautēn de Dios para moiran echousi

i18n.en: and the Rivers; and this portion they hold from Zeus—

lines.text: Πειθώ τʼ Ἀδμήτη τε Ἰάνθη τʼ Ἠλέκτρη τε
lines.translit: Peithō t' Admētē te Ianthē t' Ēlektrē te

i18n.en: Peitho, and Admete, and Ianthe, and Elektra,

notes.official: The Okeanid catalogue (349–361) — forty-one named daughters of Okeanos and Tethys — is handled as the Nereid catalogue was (240): transparent speaking-names (*Peithō* 'Persuasion', *Ploutō* 'Wealth', *Kalliroē* 'Fair-flowing', *Ourania* 'Heavenly') are transliterated as proper names, not translated. The catalogue's inclusion of soon-to-be-major figures — *Styx* (361), *Elektra* (349), *Metis* and *Eurynome* (358), *Kalypso* (359), *Dione* (353) — is left to speak for itself.

lines.text: Δωρίς τε Πρυμνώ τε καὶ Οὐρανίη θεοειδὴς
lines.translit: Dōris te Prymnō te kai Ouraniē theoeidēs

i18n.en: and Doris, and Prymno, and godlike Ourania,

lines.text: Ἱππώ τε Κλυμένη τε Ῥόδειά τε Καλλιρόη τε
lines.translit: Hippō te Klymenē te Rhodeia te Kalliroē te

i18n.en: Hippo, and Klymene, and Rhodeia, and Kalliroe,

lines.text: Ζευξώ τε Κλυτίη τε Ἰδυῖά τε Πασιθόη τε
lines.translit: Zeuxō te Klytiē te Idyia te Pasithoē te

i18n.en: Zeuxo, and Klytie, and Idyia, and Pasithoe,

lines.text: Πληξαύρη τε Γαλαξαύρη τʼ ἐρατή τε Διώνη
lines.translit: Plēxaurē te Galaxaurē t' eratē te Diōnē

i18n.en: Plexaure, and Galaxaure, and lovely Dione,

lines.text: Μηλόβοσίς τε Φόη τε καὶ εὐειδὴς Πολυδώρη
lines.translit: Mēlobosis te Phoē te kai eueidēs Polydōrē

i18n.en: Melobosis, and Phoe, and shapely Polydora,

lines.text: Κερκηίς τε φυὴν ἐρατὴ Πλουτώ τε βοῶπις
